```go
// buildStorageIntegrityArgs renders the proto block for one call. It returns
// nil only when storage integrity is disabled; when enabled the block is sent
// even with an empty table map, because the V2 contract is activated by
// version (spec 2026-09-24 H6), and it always names the reserved databases. Every Active table of the snapshot is listed;
// parts carries the promoted-but-not-yet-cleaned unsafe parts of the Active
// tables the query accesses, and is consulted only in unsafe_latest mode.
func buildStorageIntegrityArgs(opts StorageIntegrityOptions, snap sitable.Snapshot, mode ReadMode, parts map[string][]string) (*pb.StorageIntegrityArgs, error) {
	if !opts.Enabled {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if mode == "" {
		mode = ReadModeSafe
	}
	active := snap.Active()
	out := &pb.StorageIntegrityArgs{
		Tables:              make(map[string]*pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_Table, len(active)),
		ReadMode:            pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_READ_MODE_SAFE,
		ReservedRowIdColumn: DefaultReservedRowIDColumn,
		ContractVersion:     StorageIntegrityContractV2,
		// Sent on every enabled request: under V2 the engines protect these
		// databases even when no table is Active (plan A handoff).
		ReservedDatabases: sitable.ReservedDatabases(),
	}
	if mode == ReadModeUnsafeLatest {
		if opts.ReadState == nil {
			return nil, &RejectedError{Code: pb.RewriteCode_RewriteError,
				Message: "storage_integrity read mode unsafe_latest is unavailable on this housegate: no promotion-state port (co-located SNode) is wired"}
		}
		out.ReadMode = pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_READ_MODE_UNSAFE_LATEST
	}
	for _, t := range active {
		phys := sitable.PhysicalTable(t.ID)
		entry := &pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_Table{
			SafeTable:   sitable.SafeDatabase + "." + phys,
			UnsafeTable: sitable.UnsafeDatabase + "." + phys,
		}
		if mode == ReadModeUnsafeLatest {
			entry.ExcludedUnsafeParts = parts[t.ID]
		}
		out.Tables[t.ID] = entry
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

with:

```go
// buildStorageIntegrityArgs renders the proto block for one call. It returns
// nil only when storage integrity is disabled; when enabled the block is sent
// even with an empty table map, because the V2 contract is activated by
// version (spec 2026-09-24 H6), and it always names the reserved databases. Every Active table of the snapshot is listed;
// parts carries the promoted-but-not-yet-cleaned unsafe parts of the Active
// tables the query accesses, and is consulted only in unsafe_latest mode.
//
// Every Replica table (spec 2026-10-14 §11) is listed too, with SafeTable =
// UnsafeTable = hg_replica.<CopyTable> (both engines refuse an empty unsafe
// table) and no excluded parts in any mode; unsafe_latest reads of it are
// refused after the first pass (requireNoReplicaUnderUnsafeLatest), so the
// copy is never read twice. A Replica table without a copy table, or listed
// Active too, is refused.
func buildStorageIntegrityArgs(opts StorageIntegrityOptions, snap sitable.Snapshot, mode ReadMode, parts map[string][]string) (*pb.StorageIntegrityArgs, error) {
	if !opts.Enabled {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if mode == "" {
		mode = ReadModeSafe
	}
	active := snap.Active()
	served := snap.Served()
	out := &pb.StorageIntegrityArgs{
		Tables:              make(map[string]*pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_Table, len(active)+len(served)),
		ReadMode:            pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_READ_MODE_SAFE,
		ReservedRowIdColumn: DefaultReservedRowIDColumn,
		ContractVersion:     StorageIntegrityContractV2,
		// Sent on every enabled request: under V2 the engines protect these
		// databases even when no table is Active (plan A handoff).
		ReservedDatabases: sitable.ReservedDatabases(),
	}
	if mode == ReadModeUnsafeLatest {
		if opts.ReadState == nil {
			return nil, &RejectedError{Code: pb.RewriteCode_RewriteError,
				Message: "storage_integrity read mode unsafe_latest is unavailable on this housegate: no promotion-state port (co-located SNode) is wired"}
		}
		out.ReadMode = pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_READ_MODE_UNSAFE_LATEST
	}
	for _, t := range active {
		phys := sitable.PhysicalTable(t.ID)
		entry := &pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_Table{
			SafeTable:   sitable.SafeDatabase + "." + phys,
			UnsafeTable: sitable.UnsafeDatabase + "." + phys,
		}
		if mode == ReadModeUnsafeLatest {
			entry.ExcludedUnsafeParts = parts[t.ID]
		}
		out.Tables[t.ID] = entry
	}
	for _, t := range served {
		if _, isActive := out.Tables[t.ID]; isActive || t.CopyTable == "" {
			return nil, &RejectedError{Code: pb.RewriteCode_RewriteError,
				Message: fmt.Sprintf("storage-integrity table %s is listed both Active and Replica, or Replica without a copy table", t.ID)}
		}
		replica := sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + t.CopyTable
		out.Tables[t.ID] = &pb.StorageIntegrityArgs_Table{SafeTable: replica, UnsafeTable: replica}
	}
	return out, nil
}
```

In `pkg/rewriter/storage_integrity.go` (before `requireActiveAccessedIDs`, `:217`), replace:

```go
// requireActiveAccessedIDs refuses an SI-flagged accessed id that is not an
```

with:

```go
// requireNoReplicaUnderUnsafeLatest refuses an unsafe_latest read of a table
// the host serves from its member's copy (spec 2026-10-14 §11 Read modes): the
// copy holds the owner's published safe data only, and its args entry names
// the copy as both surfaces, so the first pass's rendering would read it
// twice. It runs on the first pass's accessed ids, before anything reaches
// ClickHouse, and names the first served id in sorted order.
func requireNoReplicaUnderUnsafeLatest(snap sitable.Snapshot, ids []string) error {
	owners := make(map[string]uint64)
	for _, t := range snap.Served() {
		owners[t.ID] = t.ReplicaOf
	}
	for _, id := range ids {
		if owner, served := owners[id]; served {
			return &RejectedError{Code: pb.RewriteCode_RewriteError,
				Message: fmt.Sprintf("storage_integrity read mode unsafe_latest is not available for %s: it is served read-only from a copy of indexer %d's published data; read it with SQL_x_read_mode='safe'", id, owner)}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// localizeReplicaServedUse drops the remote mapping of the target of a bare
// USE (the form forward.Plugin routes, sicore.ParseUseDatabase) when the
// query's snapshot serves that database from a member's copy (spec 2026-10-14
// §11): forward.Plugin kept the session on this host, and both engines refuse
// a USE of a remote-mapped database. A USE names no table, so no read loses
// its remote mapping; every later statement rebuilds the mapping and keeps it.
func localizeReplicaServedUse(sql string, snap sitable.Snapshot, logicalToRemote map[string]string) {
	if len(logicalToRemote) == 0 || snap == nil {
		return
	}
	db, ok := sicore.ParseUseDatabase(sql)
	if ok && slices.Contains(sitable.ServedDatabases(snap), db) {
		delete(logicalToRemote, db)
	}
}
```

In `pkg/rewriter/storage_integrity.go` (`NewStorageIntegrityScrubber`, `:293-314`), replace:

```go
// NewStorageIntegrityScrubber builds the scrubber for one snapshot: every
// Active table's qualified physical names map back to its logical id, and
// every reserved database (sitable.ReservedDatabases) and the row-id column
// are always redacted, even when no table is Active.
func NewStorageIntegrityScrubber(snap sitable.Snapshot) *StorageIntegrityScrubber {
	active := snap.Active()
	reserved := sitable.ReservedDatabases()
	// Qualified names must precede their bare database prefixes.
	pairs := make([]string, 0, len(active)*4+2*len(reserved)+2)
	for _, table := range active {
		phys := sitable.PhysicalTable(table.ID)
		pairs = append(pairs,
			sitable.SafeDatabase+"."+phys, table.ID,
			sitable.UnsafeDatabase+"."+phys, table.ID,
		)
	}
	for _, db := range reserved {
		pairs = append(pairs, db, storageIntegrityRedaction)
	}
	pairs = append(pairs, DefaultReservedRowIDColumn, storageIntegrityRedaction)
	return &StorageIntegrityScrubber{replacer: strings.NewReplacer(pairs...)}
}
```

with:

```go
// NewStorageIntegrityScrubber builds the scrubber for one snapshot: every
// Active table's qualified physical names and every Replica table's
// hg_replica.<CopyTable> map back to its logical id, and every reserved
// database (sitable.ReservedDatabases) and the row-id column are always
// redacted, even when no table is Active.
func NewStorageIntegrityScrubber(snap sitable.Snapshot) *StorageIntegrityScrubber {
	active := snap.Active()
	served := snap.Served()
	reserved := sitable.ReservedDatabases()
	// Qualified names must precede their bare database prefixes.
	pairs := make([]string, 0, len(active)*4+len(served)*2+2*len(reserved)+2)

		pairs = append(pairs,
			sitable.SafeDatabase+"."+phys, table.ID,
			sitable.UnsafeDatabase+"."+phys, table.ID,

			continue

		pairs = append(pairs, db, storageIntegrityRedaction)
	}
	pairs = append(pairs, DefaultReservedRowIDColumn, storageIntegrityRedaction)
	return &StorageIntegrityScrubber{replacer: strings.NewReplacer(pairs...)}
```
```go
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerLegWithAComputedCarrierArgumentIsRefused is Plan S3-C4 K48:
// on a peer loopback, an object-carrier callable with a computed argument is
// refused with 392, counted under computed_carrier_argument and logged once.
// The reserved-name rule runs first, so a form whose literals spell a
// reserved name (lower('HG_REPLICA')) is refused with that rule's 392.
// Literal arguments (a string or an unsigned integer), aliases that no
// carrier argument names, and carriers inside literals or comments pass, so
// the legitimate legs of peerLegForms, whose carriers take string literals
// only, keep passing (TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsPass).
func TestOnQuery_PeerLegWithAComputedCarrierArgumentIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	// Every reason is exported from startup, computed_carrier_argument
	// included, before this test's first refusal could create the series.
	if got := testutil.CollectAndCount(peerRefusals); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total has %d series before any computed-argument refusal, want every reason exported at 0, computed_carrier_argument included", got)
	}
	p := peerGuard()
	for name, form := range peerCarrierArgumentForms {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			want := "storage_integrity: a peer statement may pass only literal arguments to " + form.callable + "(); a computed database or table name is refused on a peer connection"
			if reserved, _ := PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(form.sql, sitable.ReservedDatabases(), "_hg_row_id"); reserved != "" {
				want = peerReservedMessage(reserved)
			}
			requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, form.sql, false)), want)
			if got, err := PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(form.sql); err != nil || got != form.callable {
				t.Fatalf("PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(%q) = %q, %v; want %q", form.sql, got, err, form.callable)
			}
		})
	}
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT * FROM remote('h', 'other', 'u')",
		"SELECT count() FROM remote('10.0.0.5:9000', 'phys', 'db1.u', 'user', 'pw')",
		"WITH 2 AS d SELECT count() FROM remote('10.0.0.5:9000', 'phys', 'db1.u') WHERE id > d",
		"SELECT count() FROM cluster('default', 'phys', 'db1.t', 1)",
		"SELECT count() FROM merge($$phys$$, $tag$^db1$tag$)",
		"SELECT count() FROM numbers(concat('1', '0'))",
		"SELECT merge FROM `phys`.`db1.t`",
		"SELECT 'merge(concat(1))' FROM `phys`.`db1.t`",
		"SELECT 1 /* merge(concat('hg_', 'replica')) */",
		"SELECT count() FROM merge()",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("literal carrier arguments must pass: %v", err)
			}
			if got, err := PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(sql); err != nil || got != "" {
				t.Fatalf("PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(%q) = %q, %v; want no violation", sql, got, err)
			}
		})
	}
	for name, sql := range peerLegForms {
		if got, err := PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(sql); err != nil || got != "" {
			t.Fatalf("peer leg %q: PeerCarrierArgumentViolation = %q, %v; want no violation", name, got, err)
		}
	}
	// Forwarded-from-peer and operator sessions are out of this rule's scope.
	if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, peerCarrierArgumentForms["merge of a concatenated database"].sql, true)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a forwarded-from-peer session is not peer-checked: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := PeerCarrierArgumentViolation("SELECT 'x"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("PeerCarrierArgumentViolation must return the scan error of an unscannable statement")
	}

	ctx, buf := captureLogs(t)
	before := testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues("computed_carrier_argument"))
	_ = runChain(ctx, p, peerQuery(t, peerCarrierArgumentForms["merge of a concatenated database"].sql, false))
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues("computed_carrier_argument")) - before; got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("computed_carrier_argument grew by %v, want 1", got)
	}
	out := buf.String()
	for _, want := range []string{"level=WARN", "peer statement refused by storage-integrity reserved-name guard", "plugin=sireserved", "code=392", "reason=computed_carrier_argument", "peer_address=10.0.0.7:9000"} {
		if strings.Count(out, "\n") != 1 || !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Fatalf("log = %q, want one line containing %q", out, want)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
// peerRefusal is the peer rule set (spec 2026-10-14 §14) for a rewriter
// remote() loopback, whose SQL is ClickHouse's secondary query for a leg its
// origin emitted: a statement the peer scan cannot model, every
// {name:Identifier} placeholder, and every mention of a reserved database or
// of the reserved row-id column outside comments, string literals included,
// are refused with ClickHouse 392 (not retryable). Object-carrier callables
// are not refused: a legitimate leg may carry a nested remote() that
// ClickHouse pushed into it with a JOIN or an IN subquery.
func (p *Plugin) peerRefusal(ctx context.Context, peerAddress, sql string) error {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
	if err != nil {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonStatementUnscannable, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement that cannot be checked for reserved names is refused: "+err.Error())
	}
	if identifierPlaceholderToken(surfaces.Tokens) {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement may not carry ClickHouse Identifier placeholders")
	}
	if name := reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, p.ReservedDatabases, p.ReservedRowIDColumn); name != "" {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonReservedName, name, peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: reserved name "+name+" is not addressable on a peer connection; the peer guard refuses any mention, string literals included")
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
// peerRefusal is the peer rule set (spec 2026-10-14 §14) for a rewriter
// remote() loopback, whose SQL is ClickHouse's secondary query for a leg its
// origin emitted: a statement the peer scan cannot model, every
// {name:Identifier} placeholder, and every mention of a reserved database or
// of the reserved row-id column outside comments, string literals included,
// are refused with ClickHouse 392 (not retryable). Object-carrier callables
// pass, because a legitimate leg may carry a nested remote() that ClickHouse
// pushed into it with a JOIN or an IN subquery, but only with literal
// arguments: a computed one is refused too (Plan S3-C4 K48), since it could
// name a member database such as hg_replica, which si_gateway can read,
// without the name appearing in the text.
func (p *Plugin) peerRefusal(ctx context.Context, peerAddress, sql string) error {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
	if err != nil {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonStatementUnscannable, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement that cannot be checked for reserved names is refused: "+err.Error())
	}
	if identifierPlaceholderToken(surfaces.Tokens) {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement may not carry ClickHouse Identifier placeholders")
	}
	if name := reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, p.ReservedDatabases, p.ReservedRowIDColumn); name != "" {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonReservedName, name, peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: reserved name "+name+" is not addressable on a peer connection; the peer guard refuses any mention, string literals included")
	}
	if callable := carrierArgumentViolation(surfaces.Tokens); callable != "" {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonComputedCarrierArgument, "", peerAddress, sql,
			fmt.Sprintf("storage_integrity: a peer statement may pass only literal arguments to %s(); a computed database or table name is refused on a peer connection", callable))
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
	return reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, databases, rowIDColumn), nil
}

// PeerCarrierArgumentViolation reports, on the peer scan (PeerScanOptions),
// the first object-carrier callable (IsObjectCarrierName) outside literals
// and comments, as written, whose arguments are not each exactly one string
// literal or one unsigned integer literal (Plan S3-C4 K48). ClickHouse
// constant-folds a computed argument such as concat('hg_', 'replica') into a
// database or table name, and resolves an identifier argument through the
// statement's aliases or as a tuple element, so on a peer loopback, where
// si_gateway may read hg_replica, only literal arguments pass. A call that
// never closes is a violation too. Scan errors are returned as is.
func PeerCarrierArgumentViolation(sql string) (string, error) {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return carrierArgumentViolation(surfaces.Tokens), nil
}

// carrierArgumentViolation is PeerCarrierArgumentViolation on a token stream.
// A callable is a bare or quoted carrier name directly followed by "(".
func carrierArgumentViolation(tokens []sqlsurface.Token) string {
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(tokens); i++ {
		name := tokens[i]
		if (name.Kind != sqlsurface.TokenWord && name.Kind != sqlsurface.TokenQuoted) ||
			!isPunctToken(tokens[i+1], "(") || !IsObjectCarrierName(name.Text) {
			continue
		}
		if !literalCallArguments(tokens[i+2:]) {
			return name.Text
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// literalCallArguments reports whether tokens, which follow a call's opening
// parenthesis, close the call with literal arguments only. An empty call
// passes; an empty argument, any nested parenthesis or operator, and a call
// that never closes do not.
func literalCallArguments(tokens []sqlsurface.Token) bool {
	start := 0
	for i, tok := range tokens {
		if !isPunctToken(tok, ",") && !isPunctToken(tok, ")") {
			continue
		}
		if !(i == 0 && tok.Text == ")") && !literalArgument(tokens[start:i]) {
			return false
		}
		if tok.Text == ")" {
			return true
		}
		start = i + 1
	}
	return false
}

// literalArgument reports whether arg is exactly one string literal (a
// heredoc included) or one unsigned decimal integer (a word of ASCII digits
// only). No identifier is a literal here, bare, quoted, digit-leading or
// qualified: ClickHouse's analyzer resolves an identifier argument of a
// table function through the statement's aliases before it takes it as a
// name (WITH concat('hg_', 'replica') AS d ... merge(d, '.*'), a SELECT-list
// or inline alias, an enclosing query's WITH) and d.1 as a tuple element,
// so an identifier can carry a computed name. A digits-only word is always
// that number, because ClickHouse refuses a number as an alias.
func literalArgument(arg []sqlsurface.Token) bool {
	if len(arg) != 1 {
		return false
	}
	switch arg[0].Kind {
	case sqlsurface.TokenString:
		return true
	case sqlsurface.TokenWord:
		return digitsOnly(arg[0].Text)
	default:
		return false
	}
}

// digitsOnly reports whether word is a non-empty run of ASCII digits.
func digitsOnly(word string) bool {
	if word == "" {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(word); i++ {
		if word[i] < '0' || word[i] > '9' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func isPunctToken(tok sqlsurface.Token, text string) bool {
	return tok.Kind == sqlsurface.TokenPunct && tok.Text == text
}
```

- [ ] **Step 17: Write the integration tests**

These tests pin the member-host read path end to end, through the whole server chain against ClickHouse, on the code of Steps 4, 9 and 14; they pass on first run. Without the `build.go` hunk of Step 4 (`forwardPlug.TableState` unset), every `TestReplicaReads_*` test fails at the handshake (`handshake: failed to read packet from 127.0.0.1:<port> (conn_id=1, auth_db=rrdb): read: EOF`, the hello pivoting to the owner's closed port); without Step 9's `localizeReplicaServedUse` calls, `TestReplicaReads_JoinOfTwoReplicaServedTablesReadsTheCopies` fails with `USE rrdb: code: 403, message: rewriter rejected SQL (code=UnsupportedStatement): USE target 'rrdb' is mapped to a remote upstream via dynamic_args.logical_database_to_remote_upstream_index; USE has no remote analog`.

Create `pkg/integration/storage_integrity_replica_reads_test.go`:

```go
package integration

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	housegate "github.com/housegate/housegate"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/auth"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/config"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/integration/testenv"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/network"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/sitable"
)

// The replica-read tests (spec 2026-10-14 §11, Plan S3-C4 Task 43) run a
// member host: indexer 1, storage integrity on the native engine, whose table
// state serves rrdb.a and rrdb.b from member copies in hg_replica. rrdb is
// owned by indexer 2, whose advertised HouseGate address refuses connections,
// so without serving a hello on rrdb fails and an ordinary table of rrdb is
// unreachable.
const (
	replicaReadsPhys  = "phys_rr"
	replicaReadsDB    = "rrdb"
	replicaReadsOwner = uint64(2)
	replicaReadsCopyA = "rrdb__a__i1"
	replicaReadsCopyB = "rrdb__b__i1"
)

// replicaReadsServed is the table state of a member host serving rrdb.
func replicaReadsServed() []sitable.Table {
	return []sitable.Table{
		{ID: replicaReadsDB + ".a", Status: sitable.Replica, CopyTable: replicaReadsCopyA, ReplicaOf: replicaReadsOwner},
		{ID: replicaReadsDB + ".b", Status: sitable.Replica, CopyTable: replicaReadsCopyB, ReplicaOf: replicaReadsOwner},
	}
}

// seedReplicaReads creates the two copies in hg_replica, as a member installs
// them (with the reserved row-id column), and a decoy physical table
// phys_rr.`rrdb.o` that a local read of rrdb's ordinary table o would find.
func seedReplicaReads(t *testing.T) clickhouse.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	seed := openConnNoDB(t, chEnv.Addr)
	for _, q := range []string{
		"DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS " + replicaReadsPhys,
		"CREATE DATABASE " + replicaReadsPhys,
		"CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase,
		"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyA,
		"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyB,
		"CREATE TABLE " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyA + " (_hg_row_id FixedString(32), id UInt64, v String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id",
		"CREATE TABLE " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyB + " (_hg_row_id FixedString(32), id UInt64, w UInt32) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id",
		"INSERT INTO " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyA + " VALUES (repeat('a', 32), 1, 'a1'), (repeat('b', 32), 2, 'a2'), (repeat('c', 32), 3, 'a3')",
		"INSERT INTO " + sitable.ReplicaDatabase + "." + replicaReadsCopyB + " VALUES (repeat('d', 32), 1, 10), (repeat('e', 32), 3, 30)",
		"CREATE TABLE " + replicaReadsPhys + ".`rrdb.o` (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id",
		"INSERT INTO " + replicaReadsPhys + ".`rrdb.o` VALUES (1), (2), (3), (4), (5)",
	} {
		if err := seed.Exec(ctx, q); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("seed %q: %v", q, err)
		}
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = seed.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+sitable.ReplicaDatabase)
		_ = seed.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+replicaReadsPhys)
	})
	return seed
}

// downAddress returns a loopback address nothing listens on.
func downAddress(t *testing.T) (string, uint16) {
	t.Helper()
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("reserve a port: %v", err)
	}
	port := uint16(ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr).Port)
	_ = ln.Close()
	return "127.0.0.1", port
}

// startReplicaReadsHost starts the member host (indexer 1) with state as its
// table state, the signed lane on (as on every SI host, so the rewriter
// passes writes to sitablestate) and the promotion port wired, and indexer 2
// advertised at an address that refuses connections.
func startReplicaReadsHost(t *testing.T, state sitable.TableState) *testenv.TestProxy {
	t.Helper()
	lib := requireNativeLib(t)
	signer, err := auth.NewRelaySigner(authTestKey1)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ownerHost, ownerPort := downAddress(t)
	return testenv.StartServerProxy(t, chEnv.Addr,
		testenv.WithIndexerID(1),
		testenv.WithLogicalDatabaseAt(chEnv.Database, 1),
		testenv.WithLogicalDatabaseAt(replicaReadsDB, replicaReadsOwner),
		testenv.WithStorageIntegrityReadState(&siReadStateStub{parts: map[string][]string{}}),
		testenv.WithConfigMutator(func(cfg *config.Config) {
			enabled := true
			cfg.Rewriter.Engine = "native"
			cfg.Rewriter.NativeLibraryPath = lib
			cfg.Rewriter.PhysicalDatabase = replicaReadsPhys
			cfg.Rewriter.FailOpenOnUnavailable = false
			cfg.StorageIntegrity.Enabled = &enabled
			cfg.StorageIntegrity.Ingress.Enabled = true
			cfg.StorageIntegrity.Ingress.NetworkID = "itest-replica-reads"
			cfg.StorageIntegrity.Ingress.AllowedAddresses = []string{signer.Address()}
		}),
		func(_ *config.Config, opts *housegate.Options) {
			ns := opts.NetworkState.(*network.InMemoryNetworkState)
			ns.IndexerInfos[replicaReadsOwner] = network.IndexerInfo{IndexerId: replicaReadsOwner, IndexerUrl: ownerHost, ClickhouseProxyPort: ownerPort}
			opts.StorageIntegrityTableState = state
			opts.StorageIntegrityAdmissionConsumer = &capturingConsumer{}
		},
	)
}

func queryUint64(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, sql string) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	var n uint64
	if err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), sql).Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", sql, err)
	}
	return n
}

// TestReplicaReads_JoinOfTwoReplicaServedTablesReadsTheCopies: a client of the
// quarantined owner's database, connected to the member host by hello or by
// USE, reads a JOIN of two served tables from the copies, unqualified and
// qualified, in safe mode. The copies are reachable only through their logical
// names, and an unsafe_latest read is refused with the safe-mode text.
func TestReplicaReads_JoinOfTwoReplicaServedTablesReadsTheCopies(t *testing.T) {
	seedReplicaReads(t)
	host := startReplicaReadsHost(t, sitable.NewFake(sitable.Ordinary, replicaReadsServed()...))
	ctx := context.Background()

	byHello := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, replicaReadsDB)
	if got := queryUint64(t, byHello, "SELECT count() FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id"); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("JOIN count = %d, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := queryUint64(t, byHello, "SELECT sum(id) FROM rrdb.a"); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("sum(id) of rrdb.a = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	rows, err := byHello.Query(ctx, "SELECT a.v, b.w FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id ORDER BY a.id")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("JOIN rows: %v", err)
	}
	var got []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var v string
		var w uint32
		if err := rows.Scan(&v, &w); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got = append(got, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", v, w))
	}
	rows.Close()
	if strings.Join(got, ",") != "a1:10,a3:30" {
		t.Fatalf("JOIN rows = %v, want a1 with 10 and a3 with 30", got)
	}

	byUse := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, chEnv.Database)
	if err := byUse.Exec(ctx, "USE "+replicaReadsDB); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("USE rrdb: %v", err)
	}
	if got := queryUint64(t, byUse, "SELECT count() FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id"); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("JOIN count after USE = %d, want 2", got)
	}

	// tablerefguard runs before forward and rewrite on this ordinary session.
	if err := byHello.Exec(ctx, "SELECT count() FROM "+sitable.ReplicaDatabase+"."+replicaReadsCopyA); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "reserved database hg_replica is not addressable") {
		t.Fatalf("a direct read of the copy = %v, want the table-reference guard's reserved-name refusal", err)
	}
	unsafe := clickhouse.Context(ctx, clickhouse.WithSettings(clickhouse.Settings{"SQL_x_read_mode": clickhouse.CustomSetting{Value: "unsafe_latest"}}))
	var n uint64
	err = byHello.QueryRow(unsafe, "SELECT count() FROM a").Scan(&n)
	const safeMode = "storage_integrity read mode unsafe_latest is not available for rrdb.a: it is served read-only from a copy of indexer 2's published data; read it with SQL_x_read_mode='safe'"
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), safeMode) {
		t.Fatalf("unsafe_latest read = %d, %v; want the refusal %q", n, err, safeMode)
	}
}

// TestReplicaReads_WritesAndDDLAreRefusedNamingTheOwner: every write and DDL
// that targets a served table is refused before it reaches ClickHouse, and
// the copy and the catalog are unchanged. The pinned engines refuse each of
// these statements themselves (403: a write target that maps to a remote
// upstream, or a storage-integrity table written outside the signed lane), so
// sitablestate's Replica row, the 392 naming the owner (Task 42
// TestDecide_ReplicaRows), is the second layer; a statement an engine passes
// gets that 392. Each refusal is logged for the PR record.
func TestReplicaReads_WritesAndDDLAreRefusedNamingTheOwner(t *testing.T) {
	seed := seedReplicaReads(t)
	host := startReplicaReadsHost(t, sitable.NewFake(sitable.Ordinary, replicaReadsServed()...))
	conn := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, replicaReadsDB)
	const owner = "storage_integrity: table rrdb.a is served read-only from a copy of indexer 2's published data; write through its owner"
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"INSERT INTO a (id, v) VALUES (9, 'x')",
		"INSERT INTO rrdb.a (id, v) VALUES (9, 'x')",
		"INSERT INTO a (id, v) SELECT id, toString(w) FROM b",
		"ALTER TABLE a DELETE WHERE 1",
		"ALTER TABLE a ADD COLUMN z UInt8",
		"DELETE FROM a WHERE 1",
		"TRUNCATE TABLE a",
		"OPTIMIZE TABLE a FINAL",
		"RENAME TABLE a TO c",
		"DROP TABLE a",
		"CREATE TABLE a (id UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id",
		"CREATE TABLE a ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY id AS SELECT 1 AS id",
		"CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW rrdb.mv TO a AS SELECT id, toString(w) AS v FROM b",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), sql)
			engine := err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), "code: 403") && strings.Contains(err.Error(), "rewriter rejected SQL")
			gate := err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), "code: 392") && strings.Contains(err.Error(), owner)
			if !engine && !gate {
				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want the engine's 403 refusal or the 392 %q", sql, err, owner)
			}
			t.Logf("%s refused: %v", sql, err)
		})
	}
	if got := queryUint64(t, seed, "SELECT count() FROM "+sitable.ReplicaDatabase+"."+replicaReadsCopyA); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("copy rows = %d, want the 3 installed rows", got)
	}
	if got := queryUint64(t, seed, "SELECT count() FROM system.tables WHERE database IN ('"+sitable.ReplicaDatabase+"', '"+replicaReadsPhys+"')"); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("tables in hg_replica and phys_rr = %d, want the two copies and the decoy only", got)
	}
}

// TestReplicaReads_OrdinaryTablesOfTheDatabaseStillGoToTheOwner: rrdb keeps
// its remote mapping, so its ordinary table o is read through remote() from
// the owner, which is down: the read fails rather than answering the local
// decoy phys_rr.`rrdb.o`, while the served tables still read from the copies.
func TestReplicaReads_OrdinaryTablesOfTheDatabaseStillGoToTheOwner(t *testing.T) {
	seedReplicaReads(t)
	host := startReplicaReadsHost(t, sitable.NewFake(sitable.Ordinary, replicaReadsServed()...))
	conn := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, replicaReadsDB)
	var n uint64
	err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count() FROM o").Scan(&n)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("ordinary rrdb.o answered %d from this host, want the owner's remote() read to fail", n)
	}
	t.Logf("ordinary rrdb.o while the owner is down: %v", err)
	if got := queryUint64(t, conn, "SELECT count() FROM a"); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("served rrdb.a = %d after the ordinary read, want 3", got)
	}
}

// TestReplicaReads_ServingEndedMidSessionAsksToReconnect: when the member
// stops serving rrdb, the next statement on a session kept local for it is
// refused with the retryable 733, a new hello on rrdb pivots to the owner
// (down here, so it fails), and the old session reads again once serving
// resumes.
func TestReplicaReads_ServingEndedMidSessionAsksToReconnect(t *testing.T) {
	seedReplicaReads(t)
	state := sitable.NewFake(sitable.Ordinary, replicaReadsServed()...)
	host := startReplicaReadsHost(t, state)
	conn := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, replicaReadsDB)
	if got := queryUint64(t, conn, "SELECT count() FROM a"); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("served read = %d, want 3", got)
	}

	state.Set()
	var n uint64
	err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count() FROM a").Scan(&n)
	const want = "storage_integrity: database rrdb is no longer served from a copy on this host; reconnect to reach its owner (retryable)"
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "code: 733") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
		t.Fatalf("read after serving ended = %d, %v; want 733 %q", n, err, want)
	}
	fresh := openConnDB(t, host.Addr, replicaReadsDB)
	if err := fresh.Ping(context.Background()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a new hello on rrdb must pivot to its owner, which is down")
	}

	state.Set(replicaReadsServed()...)
	if got := queryUint64(t, conn, "SELECT count() FROM a"); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("read once serving resumed = %d, want 3", got)
	}
}
```

## Task 44: housegate — agent read failover to replica hosts, release HG_TAG_P3 and HG_DIGEST_P3 (S3-C4)

Spec §11 (Agent; Host status, `replica_hosts`), contract §29.3, clarifications K46, K47 and K50. After Tasks 42 and 43 a member host answers a quarantined or unreachable owner's SI tables from its member's copies, but only for a session that reaches it. The agent picks a random permissioned indexer per session (`pkg/plugins/agent/upstream_select.go:65-109`), and when that indexer is the owner, nothing moves the session: a quarantined owner's host refuses every read of its tables with sitablestate's Refused row, code `indexer_quarantined` (`pkg/plugins/sitablestate/plugin.go:114-117`), and an unreachable owner fails the hello (`pkg/proxy/relay.go:707-723`, `:773-806`). `chproto` matches only the arbiter's write-side quarantine text (`pkg/chproto/client_error.go:96-107`), `sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo` carries no replica hosts (`pkg/registry/si_info.go:14-30`), and after its handshake the relay moves an agent session only through the SI INSERT switch inside `OnQuery` (`pkg/plugins/sistatement/switch.go:157-230`). This task:

- adds `chproto.TableRefusedMessage` (sitablestate's Refused text, now built through it byte-identically) and `chproto.IsIndexerQuarantinedReadMessage`;
- adds `replica_databases` / `replica_hosts` to `registry.StorageIntegrityInfo`, the port `registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery` and `RpcNetworkState.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts`;
- gives the relay its replica failover, `proxy.Server.UpstreamFailover`: at hello, or at an eligible read's first answer, the session is replayed on a replica host;
- adds the agent's replica tier `agent.ReplicaFailover`, its two counters and the info log `agent: replica failover`, wired by `buildAgent` for an unpinned RPC network state;
- pins the path end to end against ClickHouse: an agent of a quarantined owner's database reads the copies through Task 43's member host;
- opens the PR for Tasks 42–44, releases `HG_TAG_P3`, records the image digest `HG_DIGEST_P3`, and writes both into Appendix C.

Notes:
- **Base revisions.** housegate `origin/main` is `862a7a8`, not the header's `66d4df7`: S3-A Tasks 1–2 merged as housegate#238 (`v0.20.0`), and housegate#239–#242 changed only S3-A's plan file (so the code is `994128b`'s). Every file this task touches is byte-identical between `66d4df7` and `862a7a8` except `build.go` (S3-A's warning text, `+2` lines after `:156`) and the three docs (S3-A's peer-rule text), so the anchors below are those of `862a7a8`; where Tasks 42 and 43 move a hunk, **Files** also gives its line after them. Tasks 42 and 43 land first on this branch; where they edit the same file (`pkg/chsession/state.go`, `pkg/plugins/sitablestate/plugin.go`, `pkg/network/rpc.go`, `build.go`, the docs), the hunks below anchor on text they leave unchanged, or on Task 43's own `ReplicaServedDatabase` field (the hunk rule).
- **When a session fails over (K46).** Only in two places, both in the relay:
  - *At hello:* the dial to the session's first upstream fails, or phase 2 of its handshake does (a write or read error, EOF, an Exception or an unexpected packet instead of a ServerHello). `failoverAtHello` sends the post-plugin ClientHello, `Database` set to the session database, to each candidate in turn, binds the first that answers a ServerHello in place of the failed upstream, and the handshake continues on it unchanged (revision, raw ServerHello echo, both addenda). The client has seen nothing yet.
  - *At an eligible read's first answer:* `writeQuery` arms a `SELECT` or `WITH` of an eligible session and keeps its Query packet; `spliceClientPacket` keeps its terminating empty Data block. If the first upstream packet is an Exception the failover accepts, or the connection breaks before any packet of the query was relayed, `failoverRead` prepares a candidate completely (dial, the stored upstream hello with the session database at the client leg's revision, the same revision and timezone the client already received, the addendum, the Query and, if it was already sent, the terminator) and only then rebinds the session to it (`RebindUpstream`, which closes the owner's connection). Until then the owner stays bound, so a failover that no candidate takes lets the original Exception through and keeps the session on the owner. The candidate's first answer then decides (review round 1): `replica_hosts` is static until placement, so a reachable candidate may take the read and still not serve it (its member does not serve the database, so its host pivots to the quarantined owner and relays the same 392, or its connection breaks before it answers). Such an answer is a failure `Reason` accepts, before any packet reached the client, so `failoverRead` keeps the failover (`failoverQuery.moving`, a `readFailover` with the candidates not tried yet and the owner's original packet or error) and moves the read to the next candidate the same way. When none is left the loop handles the owner's original Exception (relayed to the client) or read error (the session ends) instead of the last candidate's answer; the session stays on that last candidate, which routes later statements as the owner's host would. The failover is reported (`FailedOver`, `agent: replica failover`, `replica_failovers_total`) only at the first answer that is not such a failure: a packet of the answer, its EndOfStream, an opaque result or an Exception `Reason` declines. A query never fails over once any packet of its answer reached the client.
- **Eligibility.** `chsession.SessionState.ReplicaFailoverEligible` is set by the relay after a handshake only when a failover is wired, and cleared by the first forwarded statement that is not a `SELECT`, `WITH` or standalone `USE` (`sicore.LeadingKeywords`, `sicore.ParseUseDatabaseStrict`), by any statement under an ownership plan (every signed INSERT lane, query-only, abort-with-success), by client Data that is not the terminator (external tables), and by a `USE` whose outcome the relay can no longer follow (a Cancel). So replaying the hello and the one read reproduces the session exactly: INSERT (INSERT … SELECT included), `SET`, DDL and `ALTER` never fail over and end eligibility for the session.
- **USE and the session database.** The replayed hello's `Database` is `SessionState.LogicalDatabaseName()` (contract §29.3) or, when it is empty, the hello's: the agent registers `sessionstate` only with the SI statement plugin (`build.go:1433`), and nothing in agent mode records a `USE` there. So the relay records the target of an eligible session's `USE` in `LogicalDatabase` at that query's EndOfStream; with a nil failover nothing is recorded. Without that, a failover after `USE other` would replay the read in the hello's database. Recorded in Appendix B.
- **The terminator and the lock.** A quarantined owner's host refuses in `OnQuery`, often before the client's terminator crossed the agent. `failoverMu` serializes the arming Query write, every client-to-upstream splice of an armed query (which also writes to the session's current upstream, not the loop's captured one) and the failover itself, so the candidate gets exactly one terminator in either order: resent from the kept bytes, or spliced afterwards. `TestAgentFailsOverAReadWhenTheOwnerIsQuarantined` pins both orders.
- **A closing session never fails over.** When the client hangs up mid-read, `runPostHandshake` closes the session and the upstream read fails; without a guard the relay dialed a candidate for a dead session and could leak its connection (measured: without the guard `TestAgentNeverFailsOverAClosedSession` fails with `candidates were asked for [db2] and reports …; this failure must never fail over`). `Relay.closing` is set before that close, and a candidate bound after it is closed again.
- **Where the port lives.** `pkg/plugins/AGENTS.md` forbids a plugin importing `pkg/proxy` (anti-patterns, and no plugin does at `origin/main`), while contract §29.3 has `agent.ReplicaFailover` implement `proxy.UpstreamFailover` with a `proxy.FailoverPhase` argument. The types are therefore defined in `pkg/plugin/upstream_failover.go` (where the relay's other ports, such as `DeferredInsertPlan`, live) and re-exported by aliases as `proxy.FailoverPhase`, `proxy.FailoverAtHello`, `proxy.FailoverAtRead` and `proxy.UpstreamFailover`, so every contract name holds. The contract's log `agent: replica failover` names `to`, which the two-method `UpstreamFailover` never learns; the relay therefore also calls an optional `FailoverReporter` (`FailedOver(ctx, database, reason, from, to)`), which `agent.ReplicaFailover` implements. Both are recorded in Appendix B.
- **Who gets the failover.** `buildAgentReplicaFailover` wires it only for an agent without `agent.upstream` whose network state implements `registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery`, which only `RpcNetworkState` does (contract §29.3), and, beyond the contract, never with a pinned upstream: the pin is the operator's explicit choice, and sistatement's own switch honours it the same way (`build.go:1573`). The contract's rule alone would wire it into every SI host's agent sidecar: the sidecar is an indexer driver pinned to its own host (`-agent-driver -agent-upstream localhost:<port>`, production `charts/sentio-node/templates/node.yaml:574-576`) whose network state is the co-located storage RPC over http (`:111-136`), and its driver traffic must stay on its own host. With the pin rule the sidecars never fail over; K47's sidecar upgrade is for the status name `replica`. Recorded in Appendix B and as a contract issue. The user's local quickstart agent (`housegate -network devnet2 -listen 127.0.0.1:9000 -si on`, no pin) gets it, which is what Task 48's drill reads through.
- **Discovery.** `StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts` asks the network-state source first and, only when it gives no decoded answer, the storage endpoint of every other indexer from `AllIndexers()` in ascending id, each endpoint once. `AllIndexers` itself is answered by the source, so with the source unreachable the lookup fails: the C4 follow-up "an unreachable indexer-a still blocks a fresh local agent's startup, though not its replica-host discovery" holds only while the source still answers `sentio_getIndexerInfos` (contract issue).
- **Metrics and log.** `clickhouse_proxy_agent_replica_failovers_total{reason}` counts a failover that reached a serving upstream (a candidate whose first answer was not a failover failure), `clickhouse_proxy_agent_replica_failover_exhausted_total{reason}` one that did not (no candidate at all included); both reasons are exported at 0 from `init`. Each served failover is logged at info as `agent: replica failover` with `database`, `owner`, `reason`, `from` and `to`; an exhausted one at warn as `relay: no replica host served the failover; the client gets the original error`. Task 48's `si_failovers` greps the first in the local agent's log.
- **Byte for byte without a failover.** With `Server.UpstreamFailover` nil the relay's wire behaviour is unchanged: the dial and handshake errors keep their texts (`exchangeUpstreamHello` carries them), no state is armed, `ReplicaFailoverEligible` stays false and no `USE` is recorded (`TestRelayWithoutUpstreamFailoverIsUnchanged`). Only the handshake's two debug lines become one.

```go
// TestTableRefusedMessageIsTheSitablestateText pins the text sitablestate
// answers for a Refused table (its plugin_test pins the same bytes from the
// gate's side), so the agent's read-side matcher and the gate cannot drift.
func TestTableRefusedMessageIsTheSitablestateText(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ id, code, reason, want string }{
		{"net1.events", "SCHEMA_INVALID", "bad column", "storage_integrity: table net1.events was refused: SCHEMA_INVALID: bad column"},
		{"net1.events", "indexer_quarantined", "storage-integrity indexer 1 is quarantined", "storage_integrity: table net1.events was refused: indexer_quarantined: storage-integrity indexer 1 is quarantined"},
		{"db1.t", "column_type", "column b", "storage_integrity: table db1.t was refused: column_type: column b"},
	} {
		if got := TableRefusedMessage(tc.id, tc.code, tc.reason); got != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("TableRefusedMessage(%q, %q, %q) = %q, want %q", tc.id, tc.code, tc.reason, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}
```

with:

```go
func IsIndexerQuarantinedMessage(msg string) bool {
	return isRefusalMessage(msg, indexerQuarantinedPrefix, indexerQuarantinedSuffix)
}

// The read side of an indexer quarantine (spec 2026-10-10 §10): the owner's
// host reports each of its SI tables Refused with the host-synthesized code
// "indexer_quarantined", and sitablestate refuses every read and write of it
// with TableRefusedMessage. The agent fails such a read over to a replica
// host (spec 2026-10-14 §11, Plan S3-C4 K46). The text is never
// session-preserving: only the arbiter's write-side IndexerQuarantinedMessage
// keeps a deferred-lane session.
const (
	tableRefusedInfix           = " was refused: "
	indexerQuarantinedReadInfix = tableRefusedInfix + "indexer_quarantined: "
)

// TableRefusedMessage is the client-facing message of sitablestate's
// refusal of a Refused table: the arbiter's refused_code and refused_reason,
// or the host's code "indexer_quarantined" and its reason.
func TableRefusedMessage(tableID, code, reason string) string {
	return tableRefusalPrefix + tableID + tableRefusedInfix + code + ": " + reason
}

// IsIndexerQuarantinedReadMessage reports whether msg, without one trailing
// SeqUnspentSuffix, is exactly TableRefusedMessage(id, "indexer_quarantined",
// reason) for a non-empty, whitespace-free table id and a non-empty reason.
func IsIndexerQuarantinedReadMessage(msg string) bool {
	msg = TrimSeqUnspentSuffix(msg)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, tableRefusalPrefix) {
		return false
	}
	rest := msg[len(tableRefusalPrefix):]
	end := strings.Index(rest, indexerQuarantinedReadInfix)
	if end <= 0 {
		return false
	}
	id, reason := rest[:end], rest[end+len(indexerQuarantinedReadInfix):]
	return strings.IndexFunc(id, unicode.IsSpace) < 0 && reason != ""
}
```

```go
	body := `{"enabled":true,"network_id":"devnet2","replica_databases":["db2"],"replica_hosts":{"db2":[0,7],"db3":[]}}`
```

Create `pkg/network/rpc_replica_hosts_test.go` (package `network`: the cache test sets the clock `rpc.now`; the file brings its own fake JSON-RPC node):

```go
package network

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"reflect"
	"strconv"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// replicaHostsNode is one fake storage-node JSON-RPC endpoint. It answers
// sentio_getIndexerInfos with indexers and sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo with
// info (a JSON object; empty answers a JSON-RPC error), and records each
// method it is asked.
type replicaHostsNode struct {
	srv      *httptest.Server
	indexers []IndexerInfo
	info     string

	mu    sync.Mutex
	calls []string
}

func newReplicaHostsNode(t *testing.T, info string) *replicaHostsNode {
	t.Helper()
	n := &replicaHostsNode{info: info}
	n.srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		var req struct {
			Method string `json:"method"`
			ID     uint64 `json:"id"`
		}
		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
			return
		}
		n.mu.Lock()
		n.calls = append(n.calls, req.Method)
		indexers, info := n.indexers, n.info
		n.mu.Unlock()
		result := ""
		switch req.Method {
		case "sentio_getIndexerInfos":
			b, _ := json.Marshal(indexers)
			result = string(b)
		case "sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo":
			result = info
		}
		if result == "" {
			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":%d,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"unavailable"}}`, req.ID)
			return
		}
		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":%d,"result":%s}`, req.ID, result)
	}))
	t.Cleanup(n.srv.Close)
	return n
}

// indexer is the IndexerInfo that advertises n as indexer id's storage RPC.
func (n *replicaHostsNode) indexer(t *testing.T, id uint64) IndexerInfo {
	t.Helper()
	u, err := url.Parse(n.srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(u.Host)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	p, err := strconv.Atoi(port)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return IndexerInfo{IndexerId: id, IndexerUrl: host, StorageNodeRpcPort: uint16(p), ClickhouseProxyPort: 9000}
}

func (n *replicaHostsNode) asked() []string {
	n.mu.Lock()
	defer n.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), n.calls...)
}

// TestRpcNetworkStateReplicaHostsAsksTheSourceThenThePeers: the agent's
// replica-host lookup (Plan S3-C4 K50) asks its network-state source first,
// then each indexer other than the owner in ascending id, and takes the first
// decoded answer, an empty one included; when nobody answers it fails with
// the contract's text.
func TestRpcNetworkStateReplicaHostsAsksTheSourceThenThePeers(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()

	t.Run("the source answers", func(t *testing.T) {
		source := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"enabled":true,"replica_hosts":{"db2":[0,2]}}`)
		rpc, err := NewRpcNetworkState(source.srv.URL, RpcOptions{})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
		if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []uint64{0, 2}) {
			t.Fatalf("StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts = %v, %v; want [0 2]", got, err)
		}
		if calls := source.asked(); !reflect.DeepEqual(calls, []string{"sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo"}) {
			t.Fatalf("source asked %v, want only sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo", calls)
		}
	})

	t.Run("the source fails, the peers answer in ascending id without the owner", func(t *testing.T) {
		source := newReplicaHostsNode(t, "")
		peerA := newReplicaHostsNode(t, "")
		owner := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"replica_hosts":{"db2":[9]}}`)
		peerC := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"replica_hosts":{"db2":[0,2]}}`)
		peerD := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"replica_hosts":{"db2":[7]}}`)
		source.indexers = []IndexerInfo{
			peerD.indexer(t, 3), peerC.indexer(t, 2), owner.indexer(t, 1), peerA.indexer(t, 0),
			{IndexerId: 4, IndexerUrl: "127.0.0.1", ClickhouseProxyPort: 9000}, // no storage RPC port
		}
		rpc, err := NewRpcNetworkState(source.srv.URL, RpcOptions{})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
		if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []uint64{0, 2}) {
			t.Fatalf("StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts = %v, %v; want indexer 2's [0 2]", got, err)
		}
		if calls := source.asked(); !reflect.DeepEqual(calls, []string{"sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo", "sentio_getIndexerInfos"}) {
			t.Fatalf("source asked %v, want the info first and then the indexer list", calls)
		}
		if calls := peerA.asked(); len(calls) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("indexer 0 asked %v, want one info call before indexer 2", calls)
		}
		if calls := owner.asked(); len(calls) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("the owner was asked %v; an unreachable owner must never block the lookup", calls)
		}
		if calls := peerD.asked(); len(calls) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("indexer 3 was asked %v after indexer 2 answered", calls)
		}
	})

	t.Run("an older server answers no replica hosts", func(t *testing.T) {
		source := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"enabled":true,"network_id":"devnet2"}`)
		rpc, err := NewRpcNetworkState(source.srv.URL, RpcOptions{})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
		if err != nil || len(got) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts = %v, %v; want empty and no error", got, err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("nobody answers", func(t *testing.T) {
		source := newReplicaHostsNode(t, "")
		peer := newReplicaHostsNode(t, "")
		source.indexers = []IndexerInfo{peer.indexer(t, 0)}
		rpc, err := NewRpcNetworkState(source.srv.URL, RpcOptions{})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		_, err = rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
		const want = "rpc: replica hosts of db2: no indexer answered sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo"
		if err == nil || err.Error() != want {
			t.Fatalf("err = %v, want %q", err, want)
		}
	})
}

// TestRpcNetworkStateReplicaHostsCachesPerDatabase: a successful answer is
// reused per database for DefaultReplicaHostsTTL and handed out as a copy; a
// failed lookup is not cached.
func TestRpcNetworkStateReplicaHostsCachesPerDatabase(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	source := newReplicaHostsNode(t, `{"replica_hosts":{"db2":[0,2],"db3":[0]}}`)
	rpc, err := NewRpcNetworkState(source.srv.URL, RpcOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	now := time.Unix(1_700_000_000, 0)
	rpc.now = func() time.Time { return now }
	infoCalls := func() int {
		n := 0
		for _, m := range source.asked() {
			if m == "sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo" {
				n++
			}
		}
		return n
	}

	first, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(first, []uint64{0, 2}) {
		t.Fatalf("first lookup = %v, %v", first, err)
	}
	first[0] = 99
	now = now.Add(DefaultReplicaHostsTTL - time.Second)
	again, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1)
	if err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(again, []uint64{0, 2}) || infoCalls() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("cached lookup = %v, %v after %d info calls; want [0 2] from the cache", again, err, infoCalls())
	}
	if other, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db3", 1); err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(other, []uint64{0}) || infoCalls() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("db3 lookup = %v, %v after %d info calls; want its own answer", other, err, infoCalls())
	}
	now = now.Add(time.Second)
	if _, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1); err != nil || infoCalls() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("expired lookup: %v after %d info calls; want a new call at DefaultReplicaHostsTTL", err, infoCalls())
	}

	source.mu.Lock()
	source.info = ""
	source.mu.Unlock()
	now = now.Add(DefaultReplicaHostsTTL)
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if _, err := rpc.StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx, "db2", 1); err == nil {
			t.Fatal("a lookup nobody answers must fail")
		}
	}
	if infoCalls() != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("info calls = %d, want every failed lookup to ask again", infoCalls())
	}
	if DefaultReplicaHostsTTL != 30*time.Second {
		t.Fatalf("DefaultReplicaHostsTTL = %s, want 30s", DefaultReplicaHostsTTL)
	}
}
```

```go
// RpcNetworkState is a read-only registry.Registry backed by a sentio
// storage-node JSON-RPC endpoint. Concurrency-safe: nextID is atomic;
// the http client is goroutine-safe; the only state held between calls
// is the replica-hosts cache, guarded by replicaMu.
type RpcNetworkState struct {
	endpoint string
	client   *http.Client
	nextID   atomic.Uint64

	// now is the replica-hosts cache's clock; nil means time.Now.
	now          func() time.Time
	replicaMu    sync.Mutex
	replicaHosts map[string]replicaHostsEntry
}

// DefaultReplicaHostsTTL is how long RpcNetworkState reuses one database's
// replica_hosts answer (Plan S3-C4 K50).
const DefaultReplicaHostsTTL = 30 * time.Second

// replicaHostsEntry is a cached successful replica_hosts answer.
type replicaHostsEntry struct {
	hosts []uint64
	until time.Time
}
```

```go
// storageEndpoint is the storage-node JSON-RPC endpoint an indexer
// advertises, with the scheme of the network-state source.
func (r *RpcNetworkState) storageEndpoint(indexerURL string, port uint16) string {
	scheme := "http"
	if u, err := url.Parse(r.endpoint); err == nil && u.Scheme != "" {
		scheme = u.Scheme
	}
	host := indexerURL
	if u, err := url.Parse(host); err == nil && u.Host != "" {
		host = u.Hostname() // tolerate a full URL in indexerUrl
	}
	return scheme + "://" + net.JoinHostPort(host, strconv.Itoa(int(port)))
}
```

```go
var _ registry.StorageIntegrityDiscovery = (*RpcNetworkState)(nil)

// StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts implements
// registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery (spec 2026-10-14 §11, Plan S3-C4
// K50). It returns replica_hosts[database] of the first decoded
// sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo answer, an empty list included (an older
// server answers none), asking the network-state source endpoint first and
// then, in ascending id, the storage endpoint of every indexer but owner, so
// an unreachable owner never blocks the lookup; every host computes the same
// map. A successful answer is reused for DefaultReplicaHostsTTL per database;
// a failed lookup is not cached.
func (r *RpcNetworkState) StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx context.Context, database string, owner uint64) ([]uint64, error) {
	now := time.Now
	if r.now != nil {
		now = r.now
	}
	at := now()
	r.replicaMu.Lock()
	if e, ok := r.replicaHosts[database]; ok && at.Before(e.until) {
		r.replicaMu.Unlock()
		return append([]uint64(nil), e.hosts...), nil
	}
	r.replicaMu.Unlock()
	hosts, ok := r.replicaHostsAt(ctx, r.endpoint, database)
	if !ok {
		hosts, ok = r.replicaHostsFromPeers(ctx, database, owner)
	}
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("rpc: replica hosts of %s: no indexer answered sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo", database)
	}
	r.replicaMu.Lock()
	if r.replicaHosts == nil {
		r.replicaHosts = make(map[string]replicaHostsEntry)
	}
	r.replicaHosts[database] = replicaHostsEntry{hosts: hosts, until: at.Add(DefaultReplicaHostsTTL)}
	r.replicaMu.Unlock()
	return append([]uint64(nil), hosts...), nil
}

// replicaHostsAt asks one endpoint; ok=false means it gave no decoded answer.
func (r *RpcNetworkState) replicaHostsAt(ctx context.Context, endpoint, database string) ([]uint64, bool) {
	var info registry.StorageIntegrityInfo
	ok, err := r.callAt(ctx, endpoint, "sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo", nil, &info)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		log.Debugw("rpc: replica-hosts lookup failed at this endpoint", "endpoint", endpoint, "database", database, "err", err)
		return nil, false
	}
	return append([]uint64(nil), info.ReplicaHosts[database]...), true
}

// replicaHostsFromPeers asks, in ascending id, every indexer but owner that
// advertises a storage endpoint not asked yet.
func (r *RpcNetworkState) replicaHostsFromPeers(ctx context.Context, database string, owner uint64) ([]uint64, bool) {
	all := r.AllIndexers()
	ids := make([]uint64, 0, len(all))
	for id := range all {
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	sort.Slice(ids, func(i, j int) bool { return ids[i] < ids[j] })
	asked := map[string]bool{r.endpoint: true}
	for _, id := range ids {
		addr := all[id]
		if id == owner || addr.Url == "" || addr.StorageRPCPort == 0 {
			continue
		}
		endpoint := r.storageEndpoint(addr.Url, addr.StorageRPCPort)
		if asked[endpoint] {
			continue
		}
		asked[endpoint] = true
		if hosts, ok := r.replicaHostsAt(ctx, endpoint, database); ok {
			return hosts, true
		}
	}
	return nil, false
}

var _ registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery = (*RpcNetworkState)(nil)
```
