p3_tool() { python3 -I -B "$T48/p3-edit.py" "$S/ledger.env" "$@"; } # p3-edit.py, the independent check of contract §32.5
p3_record() { printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$si_backup/task48-record.env"; } # $1 KEY, $2 value: one line of task48-record.env (the last line of a key wins)
p3_value() { [ -f "$si_backup/task48-record.env" ] && sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$si_backup/task48-record.env" | tail -n 1; } # $1 KEY: its last recorded value
p3_id() { case "$1" in a) echo 0 ;; b) echo 1 ;; c) echo "$INDEXER_C_ID" ;; *) echo "p3_id: a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;; esac; }
p3_installation() { case "$1" in a) echo network ;; b) echo indexer-b ;; c) echo indexer-c ;; *) echo "p3_installation: a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;; esac; }
p3_p3_image() { echo "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT_P3@$SN_DIGEST_P3"; }
p3_p2_image() { echo "ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT_P2@$SN_DIGEST_P2"; }
p3_p3_sidecar() { echo "ghcr.io/housegate/housegate:$HG_TAG_P3@$HG_DIGEST_P3"; }
p3_db() { # the acceptance database of Plan S3-B (indexer-c owns it), from the indexer-c runbook's evidence
  local db
  db="$(cat "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c/acceptance-db" 2>/dev/null)" || true
  [[ "$db" =~ ^s3eaccept[123]$ ]] || { echo "no acceptance database in $HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c/acceptance-db" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "$db"
}

p3_fresh_main() { # fails unless the live checkout is clean, detached and equal to a freshly fetched origin/main
  git fetch -q origin main || return 1
  [ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] || { echo "the live checkout has local changes; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = HEAD ] || { echo "the live checkout is not detached; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  git merge -q --ff-only origin/main || { echo "the live checkout cannot fast-forward to origin/main; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ] || { echo "HEAD holds a commit that is not on origin/main (a push the user declined?); stop and ask" >&2; return 1; }
}

p3_tests() { # the render tests: they pass with the count Step 2 recorded
  local out n
  out="$(python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py 2>&1)" || { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -n 40; echo "the render tests fail; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^Ran \([0-9][0-9]*\) tests* in .*/\1/p' | tail -n 1)"
  [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" = "$(p3_value TESTS)" ] || { echo "the render tests ran ${n:-no} tests, Step 2 recorded $(p3_value TESTS); stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "render tests: $n tests OK"
}

p3_pod() { # $1 pod: its uid, node and phase, then per container its image, readiness and restart count
  si_kubectl get pod "$1" -o json | jq -r '"pod \(.metadata.name) uid=\(.metadata.uid) node=\(.spec.nodeName) phase=\(.status.phase)", (.status.containerStatuses[] | "  \(.name) \(.image) ready=\(.ready) restarts=\(.restartCount)")'
}

p3_pod_key() { # $1 pod: its uid and every container's restart count, the identity a window must keep or change
  si_kubectl get pod "$1" -o json | jq -r '"\(.metadata.uid) " + ([.status.containerStatuses[] | "\(.name)=\(.restartCount)"] | sort | join(","))'
}

p3_container_image() { si_kubectl get pod "$1" -o json | jq -r --arg c "$2" '.spec.containers[] | select(.name == $c) | .image'; } # $1 pod, $2 container

p3_secret_refs() { # $1 pod: every Secret a container (init containers included) or a volume of the pod references, one line each, sorted
  si_kubectl get pod "$1" -o json | jq -r '
    [((.spec.initContainers // []) + .spec.containers)[] | . as $c |
      ((($c.env // [])[] | select(.valueFrom.secretKeyRef != null) | "\($c.name) \(.valueFrom.secretKeyRef.name)/\(.valueFrom.secretKeyRef.key) \(.name)"),
       (($c.envFrom // [])[] | select(.secretRef != null) | "\($c.name) \(.secretRef.name) envFrom"))]
    + [(.spec.volumes // [])[] | . as $v |
      ((select(.secret != null) | "volume:\($v.name) \(.secret.secretName)"),
       (((.projected.sources // [])[] | select(.secret != null) | "volume:\($v.name) \(.secret.name)")))]
    | .[]' | LC_ALL=C sort
}

p3_token_refs() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 none|sentio-node: the host pod references the member status token nowhere, or only from its sentio-node container as STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_STATUS_TOKEN; never the si_member password Secret
  local x=$1 r refs got
  r="sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x"
  refs="$(p3_secret_refs "$r-0")" || return 1
  got="$(printf '%s\n' "$refs" | grep -F "$r-si-member-status-token" || true)"
  case "$2" in
    none) [ -z "$got" ] || { echo "host pod $r-0 references the status token before its window: $got; stop" >&2; return 1; } ;;
    sentio-node) [ "$got" = "sentio-node $r-si-member-status-token/status-token STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_STATUS_TOKEN" ] || { echo "host pod $r-0 references the status token as: $(printf '%s' "$got" | tr '\n' ';'); stop" >&2; return 1; } ;;
    *) echo "p3_token_refs: none or sentio-node" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
  ! printf '%s\n' "$refs" | grep -qF "storage-integrity-si-v2-member-$(p3_installation "$x")" || { echo "host pod $r-0 references the si_member password Secret; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "indexer-$x: status token references: ${got:-none}; no reference to storage-integrity-si-v2-member-$(p3_installation "$x")"
}

p3_host_metrics() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 extended regexp of series names: those series of that host's embedded HouseGate registry (:9091)
  local m
  m="$(si_kubectl exec "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-0" -c sentio-node -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics)" || { echo "cannot read indexer-$1's :9091 metrics" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$m" | grep -E "^($2)(\\{[^}]*\\})? " || true
}

p3_replica_series() { p3_host_metrics "$1" 'sentio_node_storage_integrity_(member_status_up|replica_serving|replica_reads_in_flight|replica_lease_releases_total|tables)'; } # $1 a|b|c

p3_series() { awk -v s="$1" '$1 == s {printf "%.0f\n", $2; found = 1} END {if (!found) exit 1}'; } # $1 one series exactly as printed: its value from stdin, as an integer; fails when absent

p3_view_check() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 that member's ServingView JSON file, $3 mode: off (every database serving_disabled), available (owner_available), drill (the acceptance database of indexer-c served, everything else owner_available)
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "$3" "$INDEXER_C_ID" "$(p3_db)" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

x, path, mode, c, db = sys.argv[1:6]
ids = {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": int(c)}
peers = sorted(v for k, v in ids.items() if k != x)
view = json.load(open(path))
errors = []
if view.get("node_id") != f"member-{x}":
    errors.append(f"node_id is {view.get('node_id')!r}, not member-{x}")
dbs = view.get("databases") or []
owners = sorted({d.get("owner") for d in dbs})
if not dbs or not set(owners) <= set(peers):
    errors.append(f"the view covers owners {owners}, expected one or both of {peers}")
served = []
unserved = []
for d in dbs:
    name, owner = d.get("database"), d.get("owner")
    if mode == "drill" and owner == int(c) and x != "c":
        if d.get("owner_quarantined") is not True:
            errors.append(f"{name}: owner {owner} is not reported quarantined")
        elif d.get("serving") is True:
            if not d.get("tables") or not d.get("lease") or d["lease"].get("state") != "held":
                errors.append(f"{name} is served without tables or without a held lease: {json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True)}")
            else:
                served.append(name)
        elif d.get("reason") in ("owner_available", "serving_disabled"):
            errors.append(f"{name} of the quarantined owner is not served with reason {d.get('reason')!r}")
        else:
            unserved.append(f"{name} ({d.get('reason')})")
        continue
    want = "serving_disabled" if mode == "off" else "owner_available"
    if d.get("serving") is not False or d.get("reason") != want or d.get("lease") not in (None, {}):
        errors.append(f"{name} (owner {owner}) is serving={d.get('serving')} reason={d.get('reason')!r} lease={d.get('lease')!r}, expected not serving, {want}, no lease")
    if d.get("owner_unreachable") is not False:
        errors.append(f"{name}: owner {owner} is reported unreachable")
    if owner == int(c) and d.get("owner_quarantined") is not False:
        errors.append(f"{name}: owner {owner} is reported quarantined")
if mode == "drill" and x != "c" and db not in served:
    errors.append(f"the acceptance database {db} is not served")
if x != "c" and db not in [d.get("database") for d in dbs]:
    errors.append(f"the view does not list the acceptance database {db} of owner {c}")
if errors:
    for e in errors:
        print(f"member-{x}: {e}")
    sys.exit(f"member-{x}: the serving view is not as expected ({mode}); stop")
print(f"member-{x}: {len(dbs)} databases of owners {owners}; served: {served or 'none'}"
      + (f"; of the quarantined owner not served: {', '.join(unserved)}" if unserved else "") + "; every other database not serving, "
      f"reason {'serving_disabled' if mode == 'off' else 'owner_available'}, no lease, no owner unreachable")
PY
}

p3_replica_hosts_check() { # $1 a|b|c: that host's info answers replica_hosts as K50 gives it and replica_databases as given in $2 (a JSON list)
  local info
  info="$(si_info "$1")" || return 1
  python3 -I - "$1" "$INDEXER_C_ID" "$(p3_db)" "$2" "$info" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

x, c, db, want_served, info = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], json.loads(sys.argv[4]), json.loads(sys.argv[5])
hosts, served = info.get("replica_hosts"), info.get("replica_databases")
errors = []
if not isinstance(hosts, dict) or not hosts:
    errors.append(f"replica_hosts is {hosts!r}")
else:
    for name, ids in sorted(hosts.items()):
        if not (isinstance(ids, list) and len(ids) == 2 and ids == sorted(ids) and set(ids) <= {0, 1, c}):
            errors.append(f"replica_hosts[{name!r}] is {ids!r}: not two of the other SI indexers in ascending order")
    if hosts.get(db) != [0, 1]:
        errors.append(f"replica_hosts[{db!r}] is {hosts.get(db)!r}, expected [0, 1] (owner {c})")
    if hosts.get("devnet101") != [1, c]:
        errors.append(f"replica_hosts['devnet101'] is {hosts.get('devnet101')!r}, expected [1, {c}] (owner 0)")
if served != want_served:
    errors.append(f"replica_databases is {served!r}, expected {want_served!r}")
if errors:
    sys.exit(f"indexer-{x}: " + "; ".join(errors) + "; stop")
print(f"indexer-{x}: replica_hosts for {len(hosts)} databases ({db}: [0, 1]; devnet101: [1, {c}]), replica_databases {served}")
print("replica_hosts " + json.dumps(hosts, sort_keys=True))
PY
}

p3_status_is() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 database, $3 table, $4 expected status: polls si_status for up to 3 minutes
  local n s=""
  for n in $(seq 1 36); do
    s="$(si_status "$1" "$2" "$3" | jq -r .status)" || s=""
    [ "$s" = "$4" ] && { echo "indexer-$1 answers $2.$3 $s"; return 0; }
    sleep 5
  done
  echo "indexer-$1 answers $2.$3 ${s:-nothing}, not $4, after 3 minutes; stop" >&2
  return 1
}

p3_member_window_check() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 the host pod key before (p3_pod_key), after the member commit's sync: the member on the P3 image with its endpoint up and serving off, the host pod untouched
  local x=$1 m n
  m="$(si_member_pod "$x")"
  for n in $(seq 1 60); do
    [ "$(si_kubectl get pod "$m" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="si-member")].ready}' 2>/dev/null)" = true ] && break
    sleep 10
  done
  p3_pod "$m"
  [ "$(p3_container_image "$m" si-member)" = "$(p3_p3_image)" ] || { echo "member-$x does not run the P3 image; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_pod_key "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-0")" = "$2" ] || { echo "host pod of indexer-$x changed in its member window: $(p3_pod_key "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-0"), before $2; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  si_member_metrics "$x" '^sentio_node_si_member_serve_(databases|not_serving)' > "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt" || return 1
  cat "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt"
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_si_member_serve_databases{state="serving"}' < "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt")" = 0 ] || { echo "member-$x reports a serving database; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_si_member_serve_databases{state="not_serving"}' < "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt")" -ge 1 ] || { echo "member-$x reports no database: its serving endpoint is not up; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_si_member_serve_not_serving{reason="serving_disabled"}' < "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt")" = "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_si_member_serve_databases{state="not_serving"}' < "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x-window.txt")" ] || { echo "member-$x has a not-serving reason other than serving_disabled; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "member-$x: P3 image, serving endpoint up, serving off; host pod unchanged"
}

p3_host_window_check() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 the member pod key before (p3_pod_key), after the host commit's sync: the host on the P3 image and sidecar, its token refs as D29 gives them, the member endpoint reached, nothing served
  local x=$1 r h s
  r="sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x"
  h="$r-0"
  si_kubectl rollout status "statefulset/$r" --timeout=20m || return 1
  p3_pod "$h"
  [ "$(p3_container_image "$h" sentio-node)" = "$(p3_p3_image)" ] || { echo "indexer-$x does not run the P3 host image; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_container_image "$h" housegate-sidecar)" = "$(p3_p3_sidecar)" ] || { echo "indexer-$x does not run the P3 agent sidecar; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(si_kubectl get pod "$h" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "housegate-sidecar") | (.env // [])[] | select(.name == "HOUSEGATE_SI_LANES") | .value')" = off ] || { echo "indexer-$x's sidecar does not keep lanes off; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  p3_token_refs "$x" sentio-node || return 1
  [ "$(p3_pod_key "$(si_member_pod "$x")")" = "$2" ] || { echo "member-$x changed in its host window: $(p3_pod_key "$(si_member_pod "$x")"), before $2; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  for s in $(seq 1 30); do
    p3_replica_series "$x" > "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt" || true
    [ "$(p3_series sentio_node_storage_integrity_member_status_up < "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt" 2>/dev/null)" = 1 ] && break
    sleep 10
  done
  cat "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt"
  [ "$(p3_series sentio_node_storage_integrity_member_status_up < "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt")" = 1 ] || { echo "indexer-$x does not reach its member's serving endpoint (member_status_up is not 1); stop" >&2; return 1; }
  ! grep -E '^sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_serving\{[^}]*\} [1-9]' "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt" || { echo "indexer-$x serves a database Replica; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_lease_releases_total{outcome="released"}' < "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt")" = 0 ] && [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_lease_releases_total{outcome="expired"}' < "$si_backup/task48-replica-series-$x-window.txt")" = 0 ] || { echo "indexer-$x's lease counters are not both exported at 0; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  si_audit "$x" | tee "$si_backup/task48-audit-$x-window.txt"
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_mode{mode="repair"}' < "$si_backup/task48-audit-$x-window.txt")" = 1 ] && [ "$(p3_series sentio_node_storage_integrity_owner_audit_unclean_tables < "$si_backup/task48-audit-$x-window.txt")" = 0 ] || { echo "indexer-$x's owner audit is not repair and clean; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  p3_replica_hosts_check "$x" '[]' || return 1
  si_member_serving "$x" > "$si_backup/task48-serving-$x-window.json" || return 1
  p3_view_check "$x" "$si_backup/task48-serving-$x-window.json" off || return 1
  echo "indexer-$x: P3 host image and agent sidecar, member endpoint up, nothing served"
}

p3_owner_targets() { # $1 a|b|c: the HouseGate Services the member's owner probe will dial (every other SI host) exist with that port and a ready endpoint
  local y port
  for y in a b c; do
    [ "$y" = "$1" ] && continue
    case "$y" in a) port=32001 ;; b) port=33001 ;; c) port=34001 ;; esac
    [ "$(si_kubectl get service "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$y" -o json | jq --argjson p "$port" '[.spec.ports[] | select(.port == $p)] | length')" = 1 ] || { echo "Service sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$y has no port $port; stop" >&2; return 1; }
    [ "$(si_kubectl get endpoints "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$y" -o json | jq '[.subsets[]? | select(any(.ports[]?; .name == "housegate")) | .addresses[]?] | length')" -ge 1 ] || { echo "Service sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$y has no ready endpoint for its port housegate ($port); stop" >&2; return 1; }
    echo "owner probe target sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$y:$port: Service port and a ready endpoint"
  done
}

p3_serve_check() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 the host pod key before (p3_pod_key): after the serving commit's sync and 90 s: the member up with serving on, every owner available and reachable, nothing served, the host pod untouched
  local x=$1 m n
  m="$(si_member_pod "$x")"
  for n in $(seq 1 60); do
    [ "$(si_kubectl get pod "$m" -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="si-member")].ready}' 2>/dev/null)" = true ] && break
    sleep 10
  done
  p3_pod "$m"
  [ "$(p3_pod_key "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-0")" = "$2" ] || { echo "host pod of indexer-$x changed in its serving window: $(p3_pod_key "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-0"), before $2; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  sleep 90
  si_member_serving "$x" > "$si_backup/task48-serving-$x.json" || return 1
  p3_view_check "$x" "$si_backup/task48-serving-$x.json" available || return 1
  si_member_metrics "$x" '^sentio_node_si_member_serve_' > "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x.txt" || return 1
  grep -E '^sentio_node_si_member_serve_(databases|owner_unreachable)' "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x.txt"
  [ "$(p3_series 'sentio_node_si_member_serve_databases{state="serving"}' < "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x.txt")" = 0 ] || { echo "member-$x serves a database while every owner is available; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  ! grep -E '^sentio_node_si_member_serve_owner_unreachable\{[^}]*\} [1-9]' "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x.txt" || { echo "member-$x reports an owner unreachable; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(grep -cE '^sentio_node_si_member_serve_owner_unreachable\{' "$si_backup/task48-serve-series-$x.txt")" = 2 ] || { echo "member-$x does not export one owner_unreachable series per peer owner; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "member-$x: serving on, both owners available and reachable, nothing served; host pod unchanged"
}

p3_local_agent() { # the housegate on this PATH and its version line
  local bin
  bin="$(command -v housegate)" || { echo "no housegate on PATH" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s %s\n' "$bin" "$(housegate -version 2>&1 | head -n 1)"
}

p3_probe_ok() { # $1 the TSV of si_replica_grant_probe: four rows, each with got equal to expect
  python3 -I - "$1" <<'PY'
import sys

rows = [line.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for line in open(sys.argv[1]) if line.strip()]
head, body = rows[0], rows[1:]
if "expect" not in head or "got" not in head:
    sys.exit(f"{sys.argv[1]}: no expect and got columns in {head}; stop")
e, g = head.index("expect"), head.index("got")
bad = [r for r in body if len(r) <= max(e, g) or r[e] != r[g]]
if len(body) != 4 or bad:
    sys.exit(f"{sys.argv[1]}: {len(body)} rows, {len(bad)} with got != expect; stop")
print(f"{sys.argv[1]}: 4 rows, each as expected (ok, denied, denied, denied)")
PY
}

p3_copies_equal() { # si_copies_check, which must print "copies equal: <n> of <n>" with n above 0
  local out
  out="$(si_copies_check 2>&1)" || true
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$1 == "copies" && $2 == "equal:" && $4 == "of" && $3 == $5 && $3 > 0 {ok = 1} END {exit !ok}' || { echo "the members' copies are not all equal to the published entries; stop" >&2; return 1; }
}

p3_pinned_host_image() { # $1 a|b|c: the host image that host's source-image overlay pins in this checkout
  python3 -I -c 'import sys, yaml; i = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))["node"]["image"]; print(i["repository"] + ":" + i["tag"])' "k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-$1-storage-integrity-si-v2-source-image.yaml"
}

p3_replica_status_check() { # $1 a|b, $2 file of si_replica_status for the acceptance table: Replica of indexer-c with K45's four fields
  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "$INDEXER_C_ID" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

x, path, c = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
doc = json.load(open(path))
st = doc.get("result", doc) if isinstance(doc, dict) else {}
entry = st.get("owner_entry") or {}
errors = []
if st.get("status") != "replica":
    errors.append(f"status is {st.get('status')!r}")
if st.get("replica_of") != c:
    errors.append(f"replica_of is {st.get('replica_of')!r}, not {c}")
if not st.get("served_from"):
    errors.append("served_from is empty")
if entry.get("indexer_id") != c or not isinstance(entry.get("safe_block_seq"), int) or not isinstance(entry.get("applied_promotion_seq"), int):
    errors.append(f"owner_entry is {entry!r}")
if not (isinstance(st.get("frozen_since"), int) and st["frozen_since"] > 0):
    errors.append(f"frozen_since is {st.get('frozen_since')!r}")
if not st.get("schema_hash"):
    errors.append("schema_hash is empty")
if errors:
    sys.exit(f"indexer-{x}: the acceptance table's status is not Replica of indexer {c}: " + "; ".join(errors) + "; stop")
print(f"indexer-{x}: replica of indexer {c}, served_from {st['served_from']}, owner_entry {json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)}, frozen_since {st['frozen_since']}")
PY
}

p3_promotions() { si_show | jq -r '.promotion_seq | tonumber'; } # the live promotion sequence

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ runbook blocks and user scripts

p3_block() { # $1 runbook section (3.1), $2 its bash block (1 = first), $3 confirmed|read-only, then pairs OLD NEW of whole lines to replace (only the runtime placeholder lines a step names): writes the next block file, the preamble and that block of the live checkout's runbook, verbatim; prints its path and the block
  local sec="$1" n="$2" kind="$3" last num f
  shift 3
  last="$(find "$S/blocks" -maxdepth 1 -name '[0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.sh' -exec basename {} \; | LC_ALL=C sort | tail -n 1)"
  num=0
  [ -z "$last" ] || num=$((10#${last%%-*}))
  f="$(printf '%s/blocks/%03d-runbook-%s-%s.sh' "$S" $((num + 1)) "$sec" "$n")"
  {
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the preamble is written literally
    printf '%s\n' 'source "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p3-session/helpers.sh"' 'source "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p3-session/task48/task48.sh"' 'cd "$P" || exit 1'
    python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" block "$P/$p3_runbook" "$sec" "$n" "$kind" "$@"
  } > "$f.tmp" || { rm -f "$f.tmp"; return 1; }
  bash -n "$f.tmp" || { rm -f "$f.tmp"; echo "runbook §$sec block $n does not parse; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
  echo "runbook §$sec block $n ($kind) -> $f"
  tail -n +4 "$f"
}

p3_user_script() { # $1 runbook section, $2 its bash block, $3 script name: $T48/<name>, that user block of the runbook verbatim but for its key_file line, which takes the key file's path from the script's one argument; it runs once, after the marker task48-cleared-<name>
  local f="$T48/$3"
  [ ! -e "$f" ] || { echo "$f exists: a user script is written once" >&2; return 1; }
  {
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the script's lines are written literally
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' \
      "# Runbook §$1, bash block $2, of $p3_runbook at production $(git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD)," \
      '# verbatim but for its key_file line (Plan S3-C4 Task 48). Only the user runs it, once, in their own' \
      "# terminal: bash $f <key file of the devuser1 owner>" \
      '# shellcheck disable=SC1091,SC2154' \
      'set -eo pipefail' \
      '[ "$#" = 1 ] && [ -r "$1" ] || { echo "usage: bash '"$f"' <key file of the devuser1 owner>"; exit 2; }' \
      'source "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p3-session/helpers.sh"' \
      'cd "$P"' \
      '[ -e "$si_backup/task48-cleared-'"$3"'" ] || { echo "the operator has not cleared '"$3"' yet (Plan S3-C4 Task 48); stop"; exit 1; }' \
      '[ ! -e "$si_backup/task48-ran-'"$3"'" ] || { echo "'"$3"' ran already: a confirmed block never runs twice; stop"; exit 1; }' \
      ': > "$si_backup/task48-ran-'"$3"'"'
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the replacement line is written literally
    python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" block "$P/$p3_runbook" "$1" "$2" confirmed 'key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key' 'key_file="$1"'
  } > "$f.tmp" || { rm -f "$f.tmp"; return 1; }
  bash -n "$f.tmp" || { rm -f "$f.tmp"; echo "runbook §$1 block $2 does not parse; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
  chmod 700 "$f"
  echo "user script $f (runbook §$1 block $2):"
  tail -n +13 "$f"
}

p3_clear() { [ ! -e "$si_backup/task48-cleared-$1" ] || { echo "$1 was cleared before; stop" >&2; return 1; }; : > "$si_backup/task48-cleared-$1"; echo "cleared $1 for the user"; } # $1 user script name

p3_runbook_shape() { # the merged runbook holds the bash blocks this task names, of the kinds it names, and each commit block makes and records the commit this task checks
  local got want label sec n rec
  got="$(python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" map "$p3_runbook")" || return 1
  want="$(printf '%s\n' '0 r' '1.1 r' '1.2 r' '1.3 r' '2 r c' '3.1 r c r c' '3.2 r c r c' '3.3 r c r c' '4.1 r c r c r' '4.2 r c r c r' \
    '4.3 r c r c r c' '5 r' '5.1 c r' '5.2 c r' '5.3 c r' '5.4 c r' '6.1 r c' '6.2 c r' '6.3 c c' '6.4 c r' '6.5 r c' '7 r' '8.1 c c c' '8.2 c c c c c c')"
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] || { echo "the runbook's blocks are not the ones this task names:" >&2; diff <(printf '%s\n' "$want") <(printf '%s\n' "$got") >&2; return 1; }
  for label in G-b G-c G-n W-b-m W-b-h W-c-m W-c-h W-a-m W-a-h S-b S-c S-a M; do
    read -r sec n rec <<< "$(p3_stage_block "$label")"
    python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" block "$p3_runbook" "$sec" "$n" confirmed | grep -qxF "files=\"\$(si_p3_commit $label)\"" &&
      python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" block "$p3_runbook" "$sec" "$n" confirmed | grep -qxF "si_p3_push $rec \$files" ||
      { echo "runbook §$sec block $n does not commit $label and record it as $rec; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  done
  echo "runbook blocks as this task names them: $(printf '%s\n' "$got" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') sections, 13 commit blocks"
}

p3_user_scripts_ok() { # the four user blocks start with the key_file placeholder line this task replaces
  local s
  for s in '6.1 2' '6.3 1' '6.3 2' '6.5 2'; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # section and block number
    [ "$(python3 -I "$T48/p3-helpers.py" block "$p3_runbook" $s confirmed | head -n 1)" = 'key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key' ] ||
      { echo "runbook §${s% *} block ${s#* } does not start with key_file=/path/to/devuser1-owner.key; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  done
  echo "user blocks §6.1/2, §6.3/1, §6.3/2, §6.5/2 start with the key_file placeholder"
}

p3_pins_match() { # $si_backup/pins (runbook §1.1) holds exactly the ledger's values and the two local repositories
  local n v
  for n in HG_TAG_P3 HG_DIGEST_P3 CORE_TAG_P3 SN_COMMIT_P3 SN_DIGEST_P3 INDEXER_C_ID ARBITER_PIN_P2 P2_END; do
    v="$(sed -n "s/^$n=//p" "$si_backup/pins")"
    [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" = "${!n}" ] || { echo "runbook §1.1's pins give $n=${v:-nothing}, the ledger ${!n}; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  done
  [ "$(sed -n 's/^HOUSEGATE_REPO=//p' "$si_backup/pins")" = /Users/uranuswch/Dev/projects/sentio-network/housegate ] &&
    [ "$(sed -n 's/^SENTIO_NODE_REPO=//p' "$si_backup/pins")" = /Users/uranuswch/Dev/projects/sentio-network/sentio-node ] ||
    { echo "runbook §1.1's pins name other local repositories; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(wc -l < "$si_backup/pins" | tr -d ' ')" = 10 ] || { echo "runbook §1.1's pins file does not hold exactly ten lines; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "runbook §1.1's pins equal the ledger's"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the thirteen commits: preview, check, pushed

p3_stage_block() { # $1 commit label: the runbook section and bash block that commit it, and its commit record under $si_backup
  case "$1" in
    G-b) echo "3.1 2 grant-indexer-b-commit" ;;
    G-c) echo "3.2 2 grant-indexer-c-commit" ;;
    G-n) echo "3.3 2 grant-network-commit" ;;
    W-b-m) echo "4.1 2 window-b-member-commit" ;;
    W-b-h) echo "4.1 4 window-b-host-commit" ;;
    W-c-m) echo "4.2 2 window-c-member-commit" ;;
    W-c-h) echo "4.2 4 window-c-host-commit" ;;
    W-a-m) echo "4.3 2 window-a-member-commit" ;;
    W-a-h) echo "4.3 4 window-a-host-commit" ;;
    S-b) echo "5.1 1 serve-b-commit" ;;
    S-c) echo "5.2 1 serve-c-commit" ;;
    S-a) echo "5.3 1 serve-a-commit" ;;
    M) echo "5.4 1 monitoring-commit" ;;
    *) echo "unknown commit label $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}

p3_prev_stage() { # $1 commit label: the stage before it
  case "$1" in
    G-b) echo pr ;; G-c) echo G-b ;; G-n) echo G-c ;; W-b-m) echo G-n ;; W-b-h) echo W-b-m ;; W-c-m) echo W-b-h ;; W-c-h) echo W-c-m ;;
    W-a-m) echo W-c-h ;; W-a-h) echo W-a-m ;; S-b) echo W-a-h ;; S-c) echo S-b ;; S-a) echo S-c ;; M) echo S-a ;;
    *) echo "unknown commit label $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}

p3_render_check() { # $1 commit label: HEAD, that label's commit, renders exactly the objects contract §32.5 allows; a CHI commit gains one manifest line
  local x f
  case "$1" in
    G-b|G-c)
      x="${1#G-}"
      f="k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-$x-source.yaml"
      [ "$(git diff --numstat HEAD~1 HEAD -- "$f")" = "$(printf '1\t0\t%s' "$f")" ] || { echo "$1: the CHI manifest does not gain exactly one line; stop" >&2; return 1; }
      echo "$1: one line added to $f" ;;
    G-n) si_render_diff_is storage-integrity-si-v2 "changed ClickHouseInstallation/storage-integrity-si-v2" ;;
    W-[abc]-m|S-[abc])
      x="${1:2:1}"
      si_render_diff_is "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x" "changed ConfigMap/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-si-member-config" "changed StatefulSet/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-si-member" ;;
    W-[abc]-h)
      x="${1:2:1}"
      si_render_diff_is "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x" "changed ConfigMap/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x-node-config" "changed StatefulSet/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$x" ;;
    M) si_render_diff_is storage-integrity-si-v2 "changed VMRule/storage-integrity-si-v2" ;;
    *) echo "unknown commit label $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}

p3_edit_check() { # $1 commit label: in this checkout (clean, at the stage before), the runbook's si_p3_edit, checked against p3-edit.py's own edit of contract §32.5 and the render tests, committed locally as si_p3_commit commits; prints the files
  local label="$1" want files exp f
  [ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] || { echo "the checkout has local changes; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(p3_tool state | tail -n 1)" = "stage $(p3_prev_stage "$label")" ] || { echo "the checkout is not at stage $(p3_prev_stage "$label"), which $label needs; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  want="$(p3_tool files "$label")" || return 1
  exp="$(mktemp -d)"
  p3_tool apply "$label" > /dev/null || { git checkout -q -- .; rm -rf "$exp"; return 1; }
  for f in $want; do mkdir -p "$exp/$(dirname "$f")"; cp "$f" "$exp/$f"; done
  git checkout -q -- .
  files="$(si_p3_edit "$label")" || { git checkout -q -- .; rm -rf "$exp"; return 1; }
  [ "$files" = "$want" ] || { git checkout -q -- .; rm -rf "$exp"; echo "si_p3_edit $label changed $files; contract §32.5 changes $want; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # one word per file
  p3_tool same "$exp" $files >&2 || { git checkout -q -- .; rm -rf "$exp"; return 1; }
  rm -rf "$exp"
  [ "$(p3_tool state | tail -n 1)" = "stage $label" ] || { git checkout -q -- .; echo "after si_p3_edit $label the checkout does not read as stage $label; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  p3_tests >&2 || { git checkout -q -- .; return 1; }
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # one word per file
  git commit -q -m "$(si_p3_message "$label")" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" -- $files || return 1
  echo "$files"
}

p3_preview() { # $1 commit label: on a new throwaway clone of the live checkout's HEAD, that label's commit as the runbook's block will make it, checked (p3_edit_check, p3_render_check); records its tree, parent and files in task48-preview-<label>.env
  local label="$1" pv n=1 files
  rm -f "$si_backup/task48-preview-$label.env"
  [ -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ] && [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ] || { echo "the live checkout is not a clean origin/main: run p3_fresh_main first; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  while [ -e "$T48/preview-$label-$n" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
  pv="$T48/preview-$label-$n"
  git clone -q --no-checkout "$P" "$pv" || return 1
  git -C "$pv" checkout -q --detach "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  files="$(cd "$pv" && p3_edit_check "$label")" || return 1
  (cd "$pv" && p3_render_check "$label") || return 1
  git -C "$pv" show --format='commit %s' HEAD | cat
  printf 'tree=%s\nparent=%s\nfiles=%s\nclone=%s\n' "$(git -C "$pv" rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')" "$(git -C "$pv" rev-parse HEAD~1)" "$files" "$pv" > "$si_backup/task48-preview-$label.env"
  echo "preview $label ok on origin/main $(git rev-parse --short=9 HEAD) ($pv): $files"
}

p3_pushed_is() { # $1 commit label: the commit the runbook's block recorded and pushed is the previewed one, and it is on origin/main
  local label="$1" sec n name rec pv c
  read -r sec n name <<< "$(p3_stage_block "$label")"
  rec="$si_backup/$name"
  pv="$si_backup/task48-preview-$label.env"
  [ -s "$rec" ] && [ -s "$pv" ] || { echo "no $rec or no $pv: runbook §$sec block $n or the preview did not run; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  c="$(cat "$rec")"
  git fetch -q origin main || return 1
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$c" origin/main || { echo "$name names $c, which is not on origin/main (the push failed); stop and ask" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$c" ] || { echo "the live checkout is not at the recorded commit $c; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(git rev-parse "$c^{tree}")" = "$(sed -n 's/^tree=//p' "$pv")" ] && [ "$(git rev-parse "$c~1")" = "$(sed -n 's/^parent=//p' "$pv")" ] ||
    { echo "the pushed commit $c is not the previewed one ($pv); stop" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s "$c")" = "$(si_p3_message "$label")" ] && git log -1 --format=%B "$c" | grep -qxF 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' ||
    { echo "the pushed commit $c does not carry the runbook's subject and the trailer; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "$label pushed to main as $c: the previewed commit"
}

- [ ] **Step 3: Rehearsal of the runbook's thirteen commits (local only; about 15 minutes; run with `run_in_background: true`)**

On a throwaway clone of the live checkout, every commit in order made by the runbook's own `si_p3_edit` and checked against contract §32.5, with its render tests and render diff, then every revert in reverse order:

```bash
R="$T48/rehearsal"
[ ! -e "$R" ] || { echo "$R exists: an earlier rehearsal; ask before moving it aside; stop"; exit 1; }
git clone -q --no-checkout "$P" "$R"
git -C "$R" checkout -q --detach "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
cd "$R" || exit 1
base="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
for st in G-b G-c G-n W-b-m W-b-h W-c-m W-c-h W-a-m W-a-h S-b S-c S-a M; do
  files="$(p3_edit_check "$st")"
  echo "rehearsal $st: $(git log -1 --format=%s) ($files)"
  p3_render_check "$st"
done
p3_tool state | tail -n 1
prev=(pr G-b G-c G-n W-b-m W-b-h W-c-m W-c-h W-a-m W-a-h S-b S-c S-a)
i=12
for c in $(git rev-list "$base..HEAD"); do
  git revert --no-edit "$c" > /dev/null
  [ "$(p3_tool state | tail -n 1)" = "stage ${prev[$i]}" ] || { echo "rehearsal: after reverting '$(git log -1 --format=%s "$c")' the checkout is not at stage ${prev[$i]}; stop"; exit 1; }
  i=$((i - 1))
done
[ -z "$(git diff "$base" HEAD)" ] || { echo "rehearsal: the reverts do not restore origin/main; stop"; exit 1; }
p3_tests
echo "rehearsal ok: the runbook's 13 commits as contract §32.5 gives them, with their render diffs, and 13 reverts back to stage pr"
```

g="$(p3_value QUARANTINE_GENERATION)"
{

  for x in a b; do

    p3_status_is "$x" "$db" s3e_e2e replica

    p3_replica_hosts_check "$x" "$(jq -c '[.databases[] | select(.serving) | .database] | sort' "$si_backup/task48-serving-$x-quarantined.json")"
  done
  si_member_serving c > "$si_backup/task48-serving-c-quarantined.json"
  p3_view_check c "$si_backup/task48-serving-c-quarantined.json" available
  p3_replica_hosts_check c '[]'

p3_user_script 6.3 1 user-6.3-reads.sh

p3_clear user-6.3-reads.sh

**What rollback means here.** Nothing in this task is consensus-irreversible, and every change has a way back: runbook §8's blocks, each its own confirmed step with its own Gate sentence, copied with `p3_block` and run in reverse order of what ran, so that `p3-edit.py state` keeps reading a prefix of the sequence. Before a commit block ran, there is nothing to undo (a preview is a throwaway clone). During the drill (§8.3): release indexer-c first (a new copy of runbook §6.4 block 1, `p3_block 6.4 1 confirmed`), whatever else follows. After pushes, the runbook's `si_revert_p3 <commit record> <release or chi:<manifest>:<CHI>>` reverts the recorded commit on a fresh `origin/main`, runs the render tests, pushes and syncs or applies that one target (a revert that conflicts with a later commit is aborted and changes nothing); run `p3_fresh_main` from a block of this task before each:
- M: `p3_block 8.2 1 confirmed` (`si_revert_p3 monitoring-commit storage-integrity-si-v2`; the rule group goes, no pod changes).
- S-a, then S-c, then S-b: `p3_block 8.2 2 confirmed`, `p3_block 8.2 3 confirmed`, `p3_block 8.2 4 confirmed` (each member restarts with serving off and restores its held lease, revoked, from its state directory; its host stops answering Replica at its next poll, at the latest at the lease's end, and the member installs only after the release or the expiry, K44). Never revert a host commit while any member serves.
- W-a-h, W-a-m, then W-c-h, W-c-m, then W-b-h, W-b-m: `p3_block 8.2 5 confirmed` and `p3_block 8.2 6 confirmed` for indexer-a, and for x = c, then b, the same two with the line replaced, `p3_block 8.2 5 confirmed 'x=a' 'x=c'` and `p3_block 8.2 6 confirmed 'x=a' 'x=c'` (the host returns to its previous image and the `v0.15.0` sidecar in one restart and drops `replica_reads`; the member returns to `SN_DIGEST_P2`, whose decoder refuses the `serve` key the revert also removes). A host never runs the P3 sidecar without its own sync (stage-1 runbook §11 rule).
- G-n, then G-c, then G-b: `p3_block 8.1 1 confirmed`, `p3_block 8.1 2 confirmed`, `p3_block 8.1 3 confirmed` (a users reload removes each grant; the CHI manifests are applied by hand, never by helmfile, K22).

If a revert's push is refused, `si_revert_p3` has recorded nothing (`<record>.reverted` is written only after the push): drop the local revert commit with `git switch -q --detach origin/main` after a fetch, and ask again with a new copy of the block. What stays whatever is reverted: indexer-c's `quarantine_generation` two higher, indexer-a's value `5301`, row 4 of `<acceptance-db>.s3e_e2e` and their promotions; the user's local agent on `HG_TAG_P3` (it reads every earlier answer); the hosts' `replica_hosts` field returns with their images. The member status token Secrets are Plan S3-C3's and are never deleted here.

## Appendix A: binding contract (continues Appendix A of Plans S3-A, S3-B, S3-C1, S3-C2 and S3-C3)

The Appendix A sections of Plans S3-A (§0–§6), S3-B (§7–§15), S3-C1 (§16–§19), S3-C2 (§20–§24) and S3-C3 (§25–§28) stay binding, and this appendix continues their numbering. Every name below binds verbatim for every task of Plan S3-C4. A task that needs a name not listed here adds it in its own section and records it in Appendix B; it never renames one listed here.

Read first:
- **No consensus format change** (§0, §7). P3 adds no Raft command, tag, Raft-reachable field, snapshot version, header byte or feature string. `LocalNodeFeatures()` stays as `CORE_TAG_P2` has it. The voters stay on `ARBITER_DIGEST`. Each component can return to its previous image: a host to its previous host image and sidecar, a member to `SN_DIGEST_P2`.
- **Order:** code is 42 → 43 → 44 (`HG_TAG_P3`, `HG_DIGEST_P3`) ∥ 45 (`CORE_TAG_P3`) → 46 (`SN_COMMIT_P3` / `SN_DIGEST_P3`) → 47 (`P3_PR`) → 48 (`P3_END`, after `P2_END`).
- **Inert by default.** Every new knob is off by default: `storage_integrity.replica_reads`, `storage_integrity.member.serve`, `Options.StorageIntegrityReplicaReads`, `proxy.Server.UpstreamFailover`, `forward.Plugin.TableState`, and the chart values of §32. With all of them unset, every code path and every render is today's.

Names this plan consumes from earlier contracts are listed with their source in §32.9. The spelling there binds; where S3-C2 or S3-C3 fix a name differently, §32.9's consistency rule applies.

### 29. housegate (Tasks 42–44)

**29.1 Task 42: the Replica status, its gates and the in-flight counter.**

`pkg/sitable` (`sitable.go`, `static.go`, `fake.go`, new `replica_reads.go`):
- **Status:** `Replica Status` is appended after `Gone`, so `Ordinary`…`Gone` keep 0…4 and `Replica` is 5. `String()` returns `"replica"`; `ParseStatus("replica")` returns `(Replica, true)`.
- **Doc comment** (verbatim): `Replica is a table of another SI indexer that this host serves read-only from its member's copy while that owner is quarantined or unreachable (spec 2026-10-14 §11): reads and metadata are answered from hg_replica.<CopyTable>, writes and DDL are refused naming ReplicaOf.`
- **`Table` fields**, after `SchemaHash`, in this order: `CopyTable string`, commented `// Replica only: the copy's table name in hg_replica, CopyTable(ID, incarnation seq)`; and `ReplicaOf uint64`, commented `// Replica only: the SI indexer that owns the table`.
- **`Snapshot`** gains the method `Served() []Table`, commented `// every Replica table, sorted by ID`. `NewSnapshot` collects Replica tables the way it collects `active`, cloned in and out. `Static` serves none; `Fake` serves what `Set` is given.
- **`ServedDatabases`:** `func ServedDatabases(s Snapshot) []string` returns the sorted, de-duplicated databases of `s.Served()`; a nil snapshot gives nil.
- **`Schema`** keeps missing a Replica table. The rule stays: Active, Gone, Refused with a schema, and S3-A's Pending with a schema.
- **In-flight counter** (`replica_reads.go`):
  - `type ReplicaReads struct` (mutex and `map[string]int`, unexported) and `func NewReplicaReads() *ReplicaReads`.
  - `func (r *ReplicaReads) Begin(databases []string) (end func())` counts one in-flight read per listed database. `end` is idempotent; a nil receiver returns a no-op `end`.
  - `func (r *ReplicaReads) InFlight(database string) int` (0 on a nil receiver).
  - `func (r *ReplicaReads) Counts() map[string]int` (a copy, for metrics).

`pkg/plugins/sitablestate`:
- **Fields:** `Plugin` gains `ReplicaReads *sitable.ReplicaReads` and `TableState sitable.TableState`, the state rewrite takes the query's snapshot from.
- **`decide`, Replica rows:**
  - `classRead`, `classMetadata` and `classNone` allow.
  - `classWrite`, `classCreate`, `classCreateData`, `classDrop`, `classOtherDDL` and `classViewTarget` give `nonRetryable` with `CodeNonRetryable` (392) and the message (verbatim, `%s` = table id, `%d` = `ReplicaOf`): `storage_integrity: table %s is served read-only from a copy of indexer %d's published data; write through its owner`.
  - `classUnreadable` keeps its earlier refusal.
- **In-flight tracking:**
  - When `OnQuery` allows a statement and at least one accessed table answers Replica, it calls `p.ReplicaReads.Begin(<sorted unique databases of those tables>)` and keeps `end` per session.
  - **Read admission (K44).** Only after that count, `OnQuery` reads `p.TableState.Current()`. Unless it answers every accessed table that the query's snapshot answers Replica with status Replica and the same `ID`, `CopyTable` and `ReplicaOf`, the read is uncounted at once and refused with `CodeRetryable` (733) and the message (verbatim, `%s` = table id): `storage_integrity: table %s is no longer served from the copy this query was planned against; retry the query (retryable)`. A nil `TableState` with a counter admits no replica read. So a read whose snapshot rewrite took before the host published a snapshot without the database never starts after the host read `InFlight` 0 (§31.5).
  - The plugin implements `plugin.QueryCompletePlugin` (`OnQueryComplete` calls the session's `end`) and `plugin.ClosePlugin` (`OnClose` calls it).
  - Maintenance and platform-operator sessions, which return before the matrix, are not counted.

`pkg/registry` (`table_status.go`):
- `TableStatusReplica = "replica"`.
- `TableStatus` gains, after `RegistryVersion`:
  - `ReplicaOf *uint64` with tag `json:"replica_of,omitempty"`;
  - `ServedFrom string` with tag `json:"served_from,omitempty"`;
  - `OwnerEntry *OwnerEntry` with tag `json:"owner_entry,omitempty"`;
  - `FrozenSince int64` with tag `json:"frozen_since,omitempty"` (unix ms).
- `type OwnerEntry struct{ IndexerID uint64 \`json:"indexer_id"\`; SafeBlockSeq uint64 \`json:"safe_block_seq"\`; AppliedPromotionSeq uint64 \`json:"applied_promotion_seq"\` }`. These are the JSON tags of housegate `replay.TrackFrontier`.

Other housegate parts of Task 42:
- **`pkg/network`:** `RpcNetworkState.StorageIntegrityTableStatus` accepts `TableStatusReplica`. Any other unknown name stays the error `rpc: getStorageIntegrityTableStatus %s.%s: unknown status %q`.
- **Signed ingress:** `pkg/plugins/storageintegrity` is unchanged. `snapshotSchema` refuses a Replica target with its existing text `storage_integrity: table %s is not active; the signed lane admits only active tables` (392), pinned by a test.

- **`OnHello`:** in the remote branch (`info.IndexerId != p.SelfIndexerID`), when `TableState != nil` and `sitable.ServedDatabases(TableState.Current())` contains `hello.Database`, the session stays local. It calls `SetReplicaServedDatabase(hello.Database)` and logs `forward: kept a replica-served session local` (fields `db`, `owner`). Peer-trusted sessions keep their early return.

A `USE` of a database that is hosted elsewhere and not served pivots as today and clears the mark. A `USE` of a database this proxy hosts clears the mark.

A served table with an empty `CopyTable`, or whose ID is also in `snap.Active()`, is refused with `&RejectedError{Code: pb.RewriteCode_RewriteError, Message: fmt.Sprintf("storage-integrity table %s is listed both Active and Replica, or Replica without a copy table", id)}`. It fires when an object-carrier callable (`IsObjectCarrierName`) outside literals has an argument that is not exactly one string literal (heredocs included) or one unsigned integer literal (a word of ASCII digits only). Every identifier argument fires it, bare, quoted, digit-leading or qualified, because ClickHouse resolves an identifier argument through the statement's aliases (`WITH concat('hg_', 'replica') AS d SELECT * FROM merge(d, '.*')`) or as a tuple element (`d.1`).
- **Where it runs:** on peer-trusted, non-forwarded sessions, after S3-A's peer rules.

**29.3 Task 44: agent read failover and the release.**

`pkg/chproto` (`client_error.go`):
- `func TableRefusedMessage(tableID, code, reason string) string` returns `"storage_integrity: table " + tableID + " was refused: " + code + ": " + reason`. `sitablestate`'s Refused row builds its text with it, byte-identical to today.
- `func IsIndexerQuarantinedReadMessage(msg string) bool` reports, after `TrimSeqUnspentSuffix`, whether `msg` is `TableRefusedMessage(<whitespace-free id>, "indexer_quarantined", <non-empty reason>)`.

`pkg/registry` (`si_info.go`):
- `StorageIntegrityInfo` gains `ReplicaDatabases []string` with tag `json:"replica_databases"` and `ReplicaHosts map[string][]uint64` with tag `json:"replica_hosts"`. An older server's answer decodes them as empty.
- `type StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery interface{ StorageIntegrityReplicaHosts(ctx context.Context, database string, owner uint64) ([]uint64, error) }`.

`pkg/network`: `RpcNetworkState` implements `StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery`:
- **Order:** it calls `sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo` at the network-state source endpoint first, then at the storage endpoint of each indexer in `AllIndexers()` other than `owner`, in ascending id. The first decoded answer wins and gives `replica_hosts[database]`, possibly empty.
- **All failing:** when every call fails, it returns `rpc: replica hosts of %s: no indexer answered sentio_getStorageIntegrityInfo`.
- **Cache:** per database, for `DefaultReplicaHostsTTL = 30 * time.Second`.

`pkg/proxy`:
- **Interface:** `type FailoverPhase uint8` with `FailoverAtHello FailoverPhase = 1` and `FailoverAtRead FailoverPhase = 2`; `type UpstreamFailover interface{ Candidates(ctx context.Context, database string) ([]string, error); Reason(phase FailoverPhase, cause error, exc *chproto.Exception) (reason string, ok bool) }`. `Candidates` returns `host:port` addresses in order.
- **Wiring:** `Server` gains `UpstreamFailover UpstreamFailover`, passed to the relay. Nil means today's relay byte for byte.
- **At hello:** phase 2 of the handshake fails (a dial error, EOF, a read error, or an Exception instead of a ServerHello) and `Reason(FailoverAtHello, err, exc)` is ok. The relay then tries each candidate in order: dial, then the handshake with the session's ClientHello, with `Database` set to `SessionState.LogicalDatabaseName()`.
- **At an eligible read:** the query is eligible when `SessionState.ReplicaFailoverEligible` is true and the statement starts with `SELECT` or `WITH` (`sicore.LeadingKeywords`). The relay keeps its Query packet and the terminating empty Data block. If the first upstream packet is an Exception with `Reason(FailoverAtRead, nil, exc)` ok, or the connection breaks before any packet of the query was relayed to the client, the relay redials the candidates as at hello and resends both packets. The candidate's first answer is checked the same way: when it is itself such a failure, the relay moves the read to the next candidate; when no candidate is left, the client gets the owner's original Exception (or the session ends with the owner's read error) and the session stays on the last candidate. The failover is reported and counted served only at the first answer that is not such a failure (review round 1).
- **Never fails over** once any packet of the query's answer reached the client, and never for any other statement.
- **Eligibility:** `chsession.SessionState.ReplicaFailoverEligible bool` is true after hello and false from the first statement that is not `SELECT`, `WITH` or `USE`, or that carries client Data. That covers INSERT, including INSERT … SELECT, as well as `SET`, DDL and `ALTER`.
- **Metrics** (`observer.go`): `clickhouse_proxy_agent_replica_failovers_total{reason}` counts a failover that reached a serving upstream. `clickhouse_proxy_agent_replica_failover_exhausted_total{reason}` counts every candidate failing; the client then gets the original error. Both reasons are pre-exported at 0.

`pkg/plugins/agent` (new `replica_failover.go`):
- **Type:** `type ReplicaFailover struct{ Discovery registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery; Databases registry.Databases; Topology registry.Topology }` implements `proxy.UpstreamFailover` and logs through housegate `pkg/log` (`log.Infow`).
- **Reasons:** `const FailoverReasonOwnerUnreachable = "owner_unreachable"` and `const FailoverReasonOwnerQuarantined = "owner_quarantined"`.
- **`Candidates`:** the owner comes from `Databases.Get(database).IndexerId`. The ids come from `Discovery`, minus the owner and minus any id whose `Topology.ProxyByIndexerId` has `HousegatePort == 0`, in ascending order, as `Url:HousegatePort`. An empty database, a database `Databases.Get` does not know, or a discovery error gives no candidate, and the original failure reaches the client.
- **`Reason`:** at `FailoverAtRead`, an Exception that `chproto.IsIndexerQuarantinedReadMessage` matches gives `owner_quarantined`; every other Exception of a read is not ok and reaches the client unchanged. In either phase, a non-Exception failure (dial, EOF, reset, read error) gives `owner_unreachable`. At `FailoverAtHello`, any Exception also gives `owner_unreachable`, since the remote side's peer pivot failed.
- **Log** (info, verbatim): `agent: replica failover`, with fields `database`, `owner`, `reason`, `from` and `to`.
- **Wiring:** `build.go` sets `UpstreamFailover: &agent.ReplicaFailover{Discovery: discovery, Databases: reg, Topology: reg}` on the agent server only when the agent's network state implements `registry.StorageIntegrityReplicaDiscovery` (the RPC source). YAML and host-injected states keep nil.

### 30. arbiter-core (Task 45)

**30.1 Base and pins.** The branch starts from arbiter-core `origin/main` at or after `CORE_TAG_P2`. No pin changes: arbiter-proto stays at `PROTO_TAG`, and housegate at the version `CORE_TAG_P2` pins.

**30.2 Package `member/serve`** (new; files `serve.go`, `conditions.go`, `lease.go`, `probe.go`, `handler.go`, `client.go`, `metrics.go`, `BUILD.bazel` and tests).

Config and defaults:
- `type Config struct{ Enabled bool; Token string; OwnerUnreachableAfter, OwnerProbeInterval, LeaseTTL, PollInterval time.Duration; OwnerHouseGate map[uint64]string }`. `Token` is passed in by the caller from the environment and never from YAML.
- Defaults (exported): `DefaultOwnerUnreachableAfter = 60 * time.Second`, `MinOwnerUnreachableAfter = 15 * time.Second`, `DefaultOwnerProbeInterval = 5 * time.Second`, `OwnerProbeTimeout = 3 * time.Second`, `DefaultLeaseTTL = 30 * time.Second`, `MinLeaseTTL = 10 * time.Second`, `DefaultPollInterval = 5 * time.Second`, `HostDeadlineMargin = 3 * time.Second`, `DefaultListen = ":9096"` (S3-C3's `siMember.statusPort`).
- `func New(cfg Config, deps Deps) (*Server, error)` refuses with these texts (verbatim):
  - `serve: a bearer token is required`
  - `serve: owner unreachable threshold %s is below the minimum %s`
  - `serve: lease ttl %s is below the minimum %s`
  - `serve: owner probe interval %s must be at least 1s and below the unreachable threshold %s`
  - `serve: owner %d housegate address %q is not host:port`
  - `serve: Deps.StateDir is required: the server records its leases there before it grants or renews one`, and, for a lease record it cannot read, `serve: lease file %s: %v`, `serve: lease file %s has version %d, want 1`, `serve: lease file %s has a lease record without an id, a database or a ttl` and `serve: lease file %s lists database %s or lease %s twice` (review round 1)

Ports, implemented by `member.Role`:
- `type Deps struct{ Registry dataplane.RegistryView; Published Published; Copies Copies; Dial func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error); Now func() time.Time; Metrics *Metrics; Logger *slog.Logger; StateDir string }` (`StateDir`, the member's state directory, added in review round 1; `member.Role` passes `Config.StateDir`).
- `type Published interface{ Latest(ctx context.Context) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) }` gives the latest published manifest, read from the arbiter in this call and validated by the S3-C2 feed rules.
- `type Copies interface{ Databases() []OwnerDatabase; Database(owner uint64, database string) (DatabaseCopy, bool) }`.
- `type OwnerDatabase struct{ Owner uint64; Database string }`.
- `type DatabaseCopy struct{ SnapshotID string; Entry replay.TrackFrontier; Tables []TableCopy; AuditClean bool }`.
- `type TableCopy struct{ TableID string; IncarnationSeq uint64; CopyTable string; SchemaHash string; Condition TableCondition }`.
- `type TableCondition string`, with `ConditionInstalled = "installed"`, `ConditionForeign = "foreign"`, `ConditionDiverged = "diverged"` and `ConditionExcluded = "excluded"`.

Conditions are evaluated once per `PollInterval`, for every `(owner, database)` of `Copies.Databases()`. Database `d` of owner `O` is serving only while all of these hold:
1. `Enabled`;
2. O is in `Registry.View().QuarantinedIndexers`, or every probe of `OwnerHouseGate[O]` failed since a first failure at least `OwnerUnreachableAfter` ago. A probe is a TCP dial with `OwnerProbeTimeout`, every `OwnerProbeInterval`. An owner without an address only ever triggers by quarantine.
3. `e := replay.OwnerEntry(Published.Latest(), O)` equals the `e` of the previous poll;
4. `Copies.Database(O, d)` has `Entry == e` and `AuditClean`, and lists exactly the Active incarnations of `d` that `ManifestOwner` gives to O in the registry, each with `ConditionInstalled`, its seq, its schema hash and `CopyTable == sitable.CopyTable(id, seq)`.

`FrozenSince` is the first poll at which `e` was observed unchanged.

Not-serving reasons are `type Reason string`, a closed enum (verbatim):
- `owner_available`, `entry_unconfirmed`, `copy_behind`, `audit_unclean`;
- `table_foreign`, `table_diverged`, `table_excluded`, `table_missing`;
- `serving_disabled`, `feed_unavailable`, `installing`.

Leases:
- At most one lease per database. It holds an id of 128 random bits in hex, a grant time and a last renew.
- It expires `LeaseTTL` after its last grant or renew.
- A database that stops serving is revoked: renew answers 409 from then on.
- **Lease record (review round 1).** Before it answers a grant or a renew, the server replaces `LeaseFile` (`const LeaseFile = "serve-leases.json"`) in `Deps.StateDir` atomically with every lease it holds, as `{"version":1,"leases":[{"lease_id","database","owner","renewed_unix_nano","ttl_ms"}]}`. A grant or renew it cannot record is refused (500 `serve: record leases in %s: %v`) and changes nothing; a release rewrites the file without the lease. `New` restores every recorded lease that has not expired (`renewed_unix_nano` + `ttl_ms`, on the member's clock) as revoked, so after a restart renew answers 409 and `BeforeInstall` waits for the host's release or that expiry, exactly as before the restart.

Install gate:
- `func (s *Server) BeforeInstall(ctx context.Context, owner uint64, database string) error` marks the database `installing` and revokes its lease. It returns once the lease is released or expired, at once when no lease exists, or with `ctx.Err()`.
- `func (s *Server) AfterInstall(owner uint64, database string)` clears `installing`. Serving resumes only after condition 3 holds again over two polls.
- `func (s *Server) Serving() ServingView`.
- `func (s *Server) Run(ctx context.Context) error` runs the polls and the probes.
- `func (s *Server) Handler() http.Handler`.

**30.3 HTTP endpoint** (`Handler`). It is mounted by the `si-member` process on `storage_integrity.member.serve.listen` (§31). Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <Token>`, compared with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`; a missing or wrong token answers 401 `member serving: missing or wrong bearer token`. Bodies are JSON; errors are `{"error": "<text>"}`.

| Route | Request | 200 answer | Errors (verbatim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/serving` | — | `ServingView` | — |
| `POST /v1/serving/acquire` | `{"database","snapshot_id"}` | `{"lease_id","ttl_ms"}` | 409 `member serving: database %s is not served: %s` (reason); 409 `member serving: database %s moved to snapshot %s; acquire again`; 500 `serve: record leases in %s: %v` (no lease granted) |
| `POST /v1/serving/renew` | `{"lease_id"}` | `{"ttl_ms"}` | 409 `member serving: lease %s is revoked`; 404 `member serving: unknown lease %s`; 500 `serve: record leases in %s: %v` (the renew not applied) |
| `POST /v1/serving/release` | `{"lease_id"}` | `{}` (an unknown or released id also answers 200) | — |

A bad body answers 400 `member serving: %v`, and a wrong method answers 405.

The view types, with their JSON tags:
- `type ServingView struct{ NodeID string \`json:"node_id"\`; Databases []DatabaseView \`json:"databases"\` }`.
- `type DatabaseView struct`, with these fields:
  - `Database` (`database`), `Owner uint64` (`owner`), `Serving bool` (`serving`), `Reason` (`reason`);
  - `SnapshotID` (`snapshot_id`), `Entry replay.TrackFrontier` (`entry`), `FrozenSinceUnixMs int64` (`frozen_since_unix_ms`);
  - `OwnerQuarantined bool` (`owner_quarantined`), `OwnerUnreachable bool` (`owner_unreachable`);
  - `Tables []ServedTable` (`tables`) and `Lease *LeaseView` (`lease`).
- `type ServedTable struct{ TableID \`json:"table_id"\`; IncarnationSeq uint64 \`json:"incarnation_seq"\`; CopyTable \`json:"copy_table"\`; SchemaHash \`json:"schema_hash"\` }`.
- `type LeaseView struct{ LeaseID \`json:"lease_id"\`; State \`json:"state"\`; RemainingMs int64 \`json:"remaining_ms"\` }`, where state is `held` or `revoking`.

**30.4 Client** (used by sentio-node's host):
- `func NewClient(baseURL, token string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)` refuses an empty token or a URL that is not `http://host:port`.
- Methods: `(*Client) Serving(ctx) (ServingView, error)`, `Acquire(ctx, database, snapshotID string) (Lease, error)`, `Renew(ctx, leaseID string) (Lease, error)` and `Release(ctx, leaseID string) error`.
- `type Lease struct{ ID string; TTL time.Duration }`.
- Errors: `var ErrLeaseRevoked = errors.New("serve: lease revoked")`, `var ErrNotServed = errors.New("serve: database not served")` and `var ErrUnauthorized = errors.New("serve: unauthorized")`.

**30.5 Metrics** (`serve.NewMetrics() *Metrics`, `(*Metrics).Register(prometheus.Registerer) error`; exposed as `func (r *Role) ServeMetrics() *serve.Metrics` and registered by sentio-node's `simember.Run` on the si-member process's own registry, S3-C2 §24.4, Task 46). Every label value below is exported from startup, zeros included:
- `sentio_node_si_member_serve_databases{state}`, with `state` ∈ {`serving`, `revoking`, `not_serving`};
- `sentio_node_si_member_serve_not_serving{reason}`, one series per `Reason`;
- `sentio_node_si_member_serve_owner_unreachable{owner}` (0 or 1);
- `sentio_node_si_member_serve_lease_waits_total{outcome}`, with `outcome` ∈ {`released`, `expired`};
- `sentio_node_si_member_serve_revoking_seconds`, the longest current wait.

**30.6 Wiring into the S3-C2 code.**
- `member/install` keeps S3-C2's seam `Deps.BeforeInstall func(ctx context.Context, owner uint64, database string) error` (§22.3) and gains its pair `Deps.AfterInstall func(owner uint64, database string)`. Nil (both) means no wait, P2's behaviour.
- The installer calls `BeforeInstall` before installing any part of a database and `AfterInstall` after its journal write; `member.Role` sets them to `(*serve.Server).BeforeInstall` and `(*serve.Server).AfterInstall`.
- `member.Config` gains `Serve *serve.Config`. Nil means no serving endpoint, byte for byte P2.
- `member.Role` builds the `serve.Server` with adapters over the install journal (`servedCopies`, from `install.Installer.Tables`) and the feed (`publishedFeed`). It exposes `func (r *Role) ServeHandler() http.Handler`, `func (r *Role) Serving() serve.ServingView` and `func (r *Role) ServeMetrics() *serve.Metrics`.

**31.2 Host config** (`config/config.go`):
- `StorageIntegrityConfig` gains `ReplicaReads StorageIntegrityReplicaReads` with tag `yaml:"replica_reads"`.

Refusals (verbatim):

An empty `member_status_url` means no lease client and no Replica entry, exactly today's host.

New file `simember/serve.go` (S3-C2's package `simember`, §24.3):

- `simember.Run` starts it when the token env is set, and registers `role.ServeMetrics()` on the process's registry.

**31.4 Table state** (`storageintegrityadapter/tablestate`):

`model.go`:
- `type ReplicaTable struct{ TableID string; IncarnationSeq uint64; CopyTable, SchemaHash string }`.
- `type ReplicaDatabase struct{ Owner uint64; SnapshotID string; Entry hgregistry.OwnerEntry; FrozenSince time.Time; Tables []ReplicaTable }`.
- `type ReplicaSource interface{ Serving(now time.Time) map[string]ReplicaDatabase }`, keyed by database; it lists only databases whose lease is held and whose host deadline minus `serve.HostDeadlineMargin` has not passed.
- `Inputs` gains `Replicas map[string]ReplicaDatabase`.

`state.go`:
- `Config` gains `Replicas ReplicaSource`. Nil means no Replica entries.
- Every `Refresh` reads `Replicas.Serving(now)`, including one whose chain read fails. When the Replica side changed, `Refresh` republishes on the last successful chain read, as `applyRegistryWithoutChain` does for a registry change.

`snapshot.go`, in `build`:
- For each served database `d` that this host does not govern, every `foreign` key of `d` gets `sitable.Table{Status: sitable.Replica, Schema, SchemaHash, CopyTable, ReplicaOf: view.Owner}`, with the schema through `resolveSchema`. The conditions: its live incarnation is Active with `Registry.Owner == view.Owner`, and the view lists it with the same seq, schema hash and `CopyTable == sitable.CopyTable(id, seq)`.
- If any table of `d` fails these conditions, or the view lists a table the registry does not have as Active, no table of `d` is Replica, and an `Issue` names the database.
- A governed database never gets a Replica entry.

`snapshot.go`, elsewhere:
- `content` gains `replicas map[string]ReplicaDatabase`.
- `equal` also compares `CopyTable`, `ReplicaOf` and `replicas`.
- `(*Snapshot).Served() []sitable.Table`.

`status.go`:
- `StorageIntegrityTableStatus` answers Replica with `schema_json` and `schema_hash`.
- It sets the four K45 fields: `replica_of` (the owner), `served_from` (`SnapshotID`), `owner_entry` (`Entry`) and `frozen_since` (`FrozenSince` in unix ms).

Helper: `func ReplicaHosts(r Registry) map[string][]uint64` (K50).

Metrics (on the embedded HouseGate registry, `:9091`):
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_tables{status="replica"}`, a new label value of the existing series;
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_serving{database}` (1 while the snapshot answers that database Replica);
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_member_status_up` (1 while the last poll of the member endpoint succeeded);
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_reads_in_flight{database}` (from `sitable.ReplicaReads.Counts()`);
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_replica_lease_releases_total{outcome}`, with `outcome` ∈ {`released`, `expired`} and both exported at 0.

**31.5 Lease client** (new package `storageintegrityadapter/replicalease`).
- `type Config struct{ Member *serve.Client; InFlight func(database string) int; Refresh func(ctx context.Context) error; Now func() time.Time; PollInterval time.Duration; Metrics *tablestate.Metrics; Logger *slog.Logger }`, with `DefaultPollInterval = time.Second`.
- `func New(cfg Config) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client) Run(ctx) error`, and `(*Client) Serving(now time.Time) map[string]tablestate.ReplicaDatabase`, which implements `tablestate.ReplicaSource`.

Its loop:
- **Poll:** `GET /v1/serving` every `PollInterval`.
- **Acquire:** for each `serving` database without a lease.
- **Renew:** at a third of the TTL.
- **Revoked or failing:** on `ErrLeaseRevoked`, or on any failure past the local deadline, it drops the database from `Serving` and calls `Refresh`.
- **Release:** `Release` runs only after the published snapshot no longer serves the database and `InFlight(database) == 0`, read after that snapshot was published: on the poll whose `Refresh` dropped the database or a later one, with no grace poll, because `sitablestate` refuses a read whose snapshot no longer matches the current one (§29.1's read admission). It counts `released`, or `expired` when the member answered 404.

**31.6 RPCs** (`rpc/storage_integrity_info.go`, `standalone/storage_integrity_info.go`):
- `rpc.StorageIntegrityInfo` gains `ReplicaDatabases []string` with tag `json:"replica_databases"` (always present, `[]` when none) and `ReplicaHosts map[string][]uint64` with tag `json:"replica_hosts"` (always present, `{}` when none).
- The runtime fills them from `sitable.ServedDatabases(state.Current())` and `tablestate.ReplicaHosts(view)`.
- `sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus` is unchanged in shape apart from §29.1's additive fields.

**31.7 Wiring and command.**
- `standalone/standalone.go`: when `storage_integrity.replica_reads.member_status_url` is set, it creates `sitable.NewReplicaReads()` and passes it as `housegate.Options.StorageIntegrityReplicaReads`. It builds `serve.NewClient(url, os.Getenv(config.StorageIntegrityMemberStatusTokenEnv), &http.Client{Timeout: 5 * time.Second})` and the lease client (with `Refresh: state.Refresh` and `InFlight: replicaReads.InFlight`), and runs it with the table-state runtime.
- `commands/storage_integrity.go` gains `sentio-node storage-integrity member-serving --config-path <file>` (`newMemberServingCommand`). It prints the member's `ServingView` JSON to stdout, read with the token from the environment, never printed. It refuses without `member_status_url` (`storage_integrity.replica_reads.member_status_url is not set: this host has no member to ask`).

Token (D29): no new script. It is never a key of the `si_member` password Secret `storage-integrity-si-v2-member-<network|indexer-b|indexer-c>`. The same token Secret serves the host's `memberStatusTokenSecret` (on the host pod, the `sentio-node` container only) and the member's `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_MEMBER_STATUS_TOKEN`. Runbook §2 checks each token Secret by its key names only (exactly `["status-token"]`) and that no `si_member` password Secret has a `status-token` key.

Grant probe `charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_replica_grant_probe.tsv` (columns `role`, `expect` ∈ `ok` | `denied`, `statement`; the helper replaces `{copy}` with the first `hg_replica` table of `system.tables`). Its rows, in this order:
- `si_gateway ok SELECT count() FROM hg_replica.{copy}`;
- `si_gateway denied INSERT INTO hg_replica.{copy} SELECT * FROM hg_replica.{copy} LIMIT 0`;
- `si_gateway denied ALTER TABLE hg_replica.{copy} DELETE WHERE 1 = 0`;
- `si_gateway denied CREATE TABLE hg_replica.si_probe_denied (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x`.

Here `ok` means no 497 and `denied` means 497. That nothing else is granted on `hg_rstage` or `hg_member_unsafe` is proven two ways: by `test_si_gateway_reads_hg_replica_only_with_the_replica_grant` (render), and live by `si_gateway`'s `system.grants` (never `SHOW GRANTS`), which must equal its `SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS` and engine grants plus `SI_GATEWAY_REPLICA_GRANT`.

**32.6 Exit (spec §16 P3; recorded as `P3_END`).** The user's local `HG_TAG_P3` agent (upgraded by the user, D40; `local-agent-version.txt`) runs `si_agent_ch --database "<acceptance-db>" --query "SELECT count() FROM s3e_e2e SETTINGS SQL_x_read_mode='safe'"` while indexer-c is quarantined. Twelve sessions all answer the count published before the quarantine. The following are checked:
- `si_failovers` shows at least one `reason=owner_quarantined`; if none does, the 12 sessions run again, at most three rounds;
- `si_replica_status a|b` answers `replica` with `replica_of` = `INDEXER_C_ID`;
- the writes are refused 392 with the quarantine text;
- an `unsafe_latest` read is refused with the §29.2 safe-mode text;
- after the release, both members stop serving with reason `owner_available` and the hosts answer the table `ordinary` again.

- Relay fires OnQueryComplete exactly once per client Query, including when the OnQuery chain rejects it. It refuses a pipelined Query while another is still active, so one end slot per session is safe. OnQueryComplete uses the same chain filters as OnQuery, and OnClose runs every close plugin.
- sitablestate registers its complete and close hooks only when Options.StorageIntegrityReplicaReads is set. Unset, the chain is exactly today's.
- Maintenance and platform-operator sessions bypass rewrite (their SQL is forwarded verbatim), so they never read hg_replica copies. Not counting them, as the contract says, is safe.
- A query takes its table snapshot in the rewrite plugin (pkg/plugins/rewrite/rewriter.go:147), before sitablestate counts it. The drafted one-poll grace of Task 46's lease client did not bound that gap (a rewrite can outlast a poll); sitablestate's read admission (count, then check TableState.Current()) replaced it in review round 1. Task 42's Consumed-by section and Notes record this.

### Task 48

- Task 48 runs the merged runbook docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p3-replica-reads.md §1–§7 one block at a time. Each block is copied byte for byte into a block file by p3_block, and only named placeholder lines are replaced: the §1.1 clone line and the §8.2 x=a line. The runbook decides every check, helper, commit edit, value and evidence name (D19), which is the pattern of S3-C3 Task 41.
- The thirteen single-service commits of contract §32.5 are made and pushed only by the runbook's own confirmed blocks (si_p3_commit/si_p3_edit/si_p3_push). Before each push, p3_preview makes the same commit with si_p3_edit on a throwaway clone at the same origin/main. It then checks that commit with p3-edit.py: the right files, the stage before and after, and content equal to contract §32.5 (YAML documents and Python AST, so comments may differ). It also runs the render tests and si_render_diff_is, and records the commit's tree. After the push, p3_pushed_is checks the pushed commit's tree, parent, subject and trailer against the preview.
- Step 1 runs p3_runbook_shape, which pins the runbook's block layout: 24 sections with each block's kind, the 13 commit blocks with their labels and commit records, and the 4 user blocks with their key_file placeholder. If Task 47 changes its runbook, Step 1 stops.
- The drill values now come from the runbook: baseline row (4, 'p3-6.1-4'), refused row (5, 'p3-6.3-refused'), and indexer-a's 5301. r3's 'p3-baseline' and 'p3-refused' labels and its own drill scripts are gone. The user's four blocks (§6.1/2, §6.3/1, §6.3/2, §6.5/2) become one-shot scripts. Each is verbatim except its key_file line, which takes the key path as an argument, and runs only once a marker clears it.
- How a failed commit block is handled: if main moved, si_p3_commit refuses before committing. If the render tests or si_head_is fail after the local commit, that commit is dropped. If the push itself is refused, si_p3_push has already written the record, so p3_pushed_is reports it; the record is moved aside only on the user's word, and then the agent previews again and asks again. A push is never forced.
- Task 48's own read-only checks, kept from r3, wrap each window: host and member pod restarts, the D29 token references of every host-pod container and volume, serving views, the K50 replica_hosts map, owner-probe targets, vmalert rules and alerts, generation and frontier checks around the quarantine and release, the budget, and the p3-end.txt record.
- Structure: 23 steps. Each grant, window, serving or monitoring window ends the turn. Steps 22–23 are the docs-only record PR and the Appendix C record of P3_END with the run record 'P3 run' (R1–R4 through s3-ledger.py).
